Dear AWA People & Culture Team,

I’m writing to join AWA’s Talent Network because your work sits exactly where my experience and my heart meet: helping young people and their families through some of the hardest moments of their lives.

For more than 25 years, I have designed and facilitated learning programs, coached leaders and individuals, and coordinated group programs in person and online, in English and in Spanish. Early in my career in Venezuela, I co-facilitated a community prevention program for adolescents sponsored by Empresas Polar, with workshops on substance use and teen pregnancy prevention for teens living near the company’s facilities. That experience showed me how much prevention depends on reaching families in their own language and reality.

This work is also personal. Addiction to alcohol and drugs has touched my own family, and I have lost a young family member to its consequences. I now have four young grandchildren, and the idea of contributing to prevention efforts that protect children like them means a great deal to me.

I believe I could add value to AWA by supporting staff training and onboarding, developing educational workshops for families, especially Spanish-speaking families, or helping coordinate programs so that teens and parents stay engaged and informed. I’m based in Miami, fully bilingual, and comfortable working remotely or on-site in Miami.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to learn how I could support your team and the families you serve.

Warm regards,
Esther Leon
(713) 504-7640 · leoncesther@gmail.com · linkedin.com/in/esther-leon-ld

I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. With over five years of leadership experience in clinical settings, I have successfully supervised multidisciplinary teams and managed programs focused on delivering high-quality care to adolescents and families.

In my current role as Clinical Director at Hope Haven Inc., I oversee a team of approximately 20 staff members, ensuring compliance with CARF standards while fostering a trauma-informed environment. My background includes developing treatment plans, conducting crisis interventions, and maintaining documentation quality, which are crucial for the success of your new facility in North Carolina. I am particularly drawn to your values of kindness, growth, and optimism, which resonate with my leadership philosophy. I am eager to contribute to the launch and ongoing success of your clinic, ensuring that we not only meet but exceed the expectations of the adolescents and families we serve.

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and vision can support the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Dear Hiring Manager,

Your posting for a Utilization Review Specialist asks for someone who can keep complex authorizations accurate, documented, and on deadline so that adolescents and families can stay connected to treatment. I want to be upfront: my background is in UI design and enterprise software rather than behavioral health utilization review, and I do not have PHP/IOP authorization experience. I am writing because the detail-oriented, system-driven work this role demands is work I have done in a different setting, and I would like you to weigh that honestly.

In 2024, I worked as a UI Designer on SAP's analytics products, designing interfaces for enterprise software used for data tracking and reporting. That work meant understanding how people record, monitor, and retrieve structured information inside large systems, which is directly relevant to your need for accurate authorization records, tracked units, coverage dates, and payer deadlines in an EMR/EHR. I am comfortable learning new platforms quickly and keeping meticulous records, and I would approach Kipu or any authorization software with that same discipline.

My CCNA certification from Cisco reflects a structured, rules-based way of working: following technical standards precisely and troubleshooting methodically. I would bring the same rigor to learning ASAM, LOCUS, and CALOCUS criteria and to documenting medical necessity clearly. I am fluent in English and French at C2 level, so clear written and verbal communication with payers, clinical teams, and admissions staff comes naturally to me. I also work well independently from a remote setting. I am based in France and open to remote roles, and I am flexible on hours and willing to complete the required background screening and reference checks.

I understand that the role requires 2+ years of behavioral health UR experience, and I recognize I do not meet that requirement today. If there is room in your team for someone with strong systems skills who is committed to building this expertise, I would welcome the conversation. You can reach me at mark.james@agenticareer.com. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Mark James

**Behavioral Health Utilization Review Specialist | Clinical Documentation | Care Coordination**

San Clemente, CA | 949-677-0306 | cristyfish@gmail.com

**Seeking Full-Time Remote Opportunities**

## PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY

Experienced behavioral health professional and Certified Addiction Treatment Counselor III (CATC III) with more than six years of experience in mental health, substance use disorder, and co-occurring disorder treatment settings. Extensive background in clinical documentation, biopsychosocial assessments, treatment planning, progress evaluations, discharge planning, and utilization review support. Knowledgeable in detoxification, residential treatment (RTC), partial hospitalization (PHP), and intensive outpatient (IOP) levels of care. Skilled in collaborating with multidisciplinary treatment teams, documenting clinical progress, identifying barriers to continued treatment, and supporting appropriate levels of care. - Behavioral Health Utilization Review Support

candidates.summary: I have over 7 years of experience in U.S. medical billing and Revenue Cycle Management (RCM), specializing in insurance AR follow-up, claims processing, denial management, appeals, payment posting, and reimbursement resolution. I have worked with Medicare, Medicaid, Medi-Cal, and commercial insurance payers. My technical experience includes Epic, Cerner, Meditech, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, CureMD, AdvancedMD, Prompt EMR, and other billing platforms. I am skilled in researching payer requirements, resolving complex claim issues, managing aging accounts, and handling 30+ claims per day while maintaining accuracy and productivity. I am seeking a fully remote opportunity where I can contribute my RCM knowledge, analytical skills, and problem-solving abilities.

work_history.title: Revenue Cycle Specialist
work_history.summary:
•	Confirm detailed insurance coverage, including commercial, Medicare/Medicaid, Workers’ Compensation, and Personal Injury cases by verifying policy status, benefits, coordination of benefits, adjuster or attorney information, and authorization requirements before services are rendered.
•	Accurately submit professional and institutional claims using CMS-1500 and UB-04 forms Prepare, code, and transmit clean claims to insurance payers and third-party administrators, ensuring compliance with payer-specific billing rules and timelines, including special formats required for WC and PI claims.
•	Identify and correct claim errors prior to submission to reduce denials and rejections, Conduct thorough claim audits to catch issues such as missing authorizations, incorrect codes, or mismatched patient demographics. Coordinate with providers and front-office staff to correct and finalize claims before submission through clearinghouses.
•	Follow up diligently on unpaid, delayed, or underpaid claims to ensure timely resolution proactively monitor claims aging reports and take immediate action on claims not paid within standard timelines. Contact insurance carriers, TPAs, or attorneys directly, document conversations, and escalate unresolved issues as necessary.
•	Handle denials and rejections by investigating root causes and initiating appeals
Work rejected or denied claims by identifying the underlying issue (e.g., coding, authorization, documentation). File structured appeals with necessary medical records, chart notes, or legal releases, and track the appeal status until resolution.
•	Interpret and reconcile Explanation of Benefits (EOBs) and Electronic Remittance Advice (ERAs) Analyze payment data, verify contractual adjustments, and post accurate payments to patient accounts. Identify variances in expected versus received payments and take corrective action on discrepancies. Post insurance and patient payments, adjustments, and write-offs with accuracy, record payments into billing systems based on EOBs, patient payments, or legal settlements, ensuring correct application to accounts and proper financial reconciliation of balances.
•	Manage and track appeals for denied claims with detailed follow-up
Draft customized appeal letters, collect all necessary supporting documentation, and maintain a tracking log to follow up on appeals and reprocess claims successful.
•	Contact patients to explain balances, insurance coverage, and payment responsibilities provide patient education regarding their financial responsibilities, deductibles, copays, and payment options. Assist patients in setting up payment plans or answering questions regarding settlement-related claims.

work_history.title: Medical Billing Specialist
work_history.summary:
•	Responsible for entering medical charges accurately using appropriate CPT, ICD-10, and modifier codes, ensuring that each claim reflects the services provided and complies with payer-specific billing rules and coding guidelines.
•	Submit insurance claims efficiently through clearinghouses or directly on payer websites, maintaining a consistent workflow to prevent billing delays and maximize timely reimbursement.
•	Closely monitor all claims after submission to identify rejections or transmission errors; take immediate action to correct and resubmit claims to avoid cash flow disruption.
•	Accurately post payments from insurance companies and patients by reviewing EOBs (Explanation of Benefits) and ERAs (Electronic Remittance Advice), applying contractual adjustments, and identifying discrepancies or underpayments for follow-up.
•	Investigate unpaid or underpaid claims by contacting insurance carriers, gathering necessary documentation, and resolving issues through timely and professional communication.
•	Analyze and respond to insurance denials by determining the root cause, obtaining clinical notes or additional documents when required, and submitting well-supported appeals or reconsideration requests.
•	Ensure all patient account information is kept up to date in the billing system, including demographic details, insurance policies, and coverage changes, to avoid billing errors and rejections.
•	Provide clear and empathetic assistance to patients regarding their billing questions, explaining balances, offering payment options, and resolving any confusion related to insurance payments or statements.
•	Maintain compliance with federal healthcare regulations, including HIPAA, and adhere to payer guidelines to protect patient privacy and ensure all billing activity is legally sound.
•	Proactively communicate with internal teams such as scheduling, front desk, and clinical staff to prevent billing disruptions caused by missing authorizations, incorrect insurance details, or incomplete charge capture.
•	Keep detailed records of all billing activities, including payment tracking, denial resolutions, appeal statuses, and patient communications, ensuring proper documentation for auditing and reporting purposes.
•	Contribute to internal audits and reporting by identifying common trends in denials or payment delays and suggesting workflow improvements that can enhance billing accuracy and efficiency.

I'm a Certified Behavioral Health Case Manager, with a Psychology degree from the University of Miami, and over three years of experience handling clinical file audits, insurance authorizations, and case management. I’d love to help keep your clients' care moving without delays as your company's new Utilization Review Specialist.

Right now, I work as a Housing Program Coordinator and Case Manager at Lotus House. My day-to-day is a mix of direct client support such as helping individuals manage depression and stabilize their health to heavy administrative review. I manage a high-volume caseload, verify Medicaid and Medicare coverage, run LOCUS risk assessments to track progress over time, and proactively audit clinical documentation to catch missing criteria before it leads to service or authorization delays. When denials do happen, I help clients and care teams navigate the gaps.

Before Lotus House, I worked remotely as a Compliance and Document Review Specialist for Miami-Dade County’s Emergency Rental Assistance Program, reviewing high-stakes applications against strict policy rules under tight deadlines. Between that, my research work at University of Miami, and daily EHR/HMIS tracking, I’m comfortable managing my own queue and staying organized while working remotely.

I’m familiar with DSM-5 and ASAM/LOCUS criteria, and I know how important clear, timely communication between clinical staff and insurance payers is for keeping treatment on track. Thank you so much for considering my application - I’d welcome the chance to talk more about how I can support your team!

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator position with your PHP and IOP programs. As an art educator, experienced teacher, and graduate student in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a specialization in Play Therapy, I have built my career around exactly what this role describes: using creative, process-based experiences to help young people express themselves, regulate their emotions, and discover their own capacity to grow.

Over the past couple of years, I have taught process-based art to children and adolescents in a variety of settings. At artNEST Studios, I facilitated weekly after-school art programs for elementary students, designing curriculum that intentionally prioritized creative exploration over the final product. This approach gives participants permission to take risks, make mistakes, and express themselves authentically. I also managed full-cycle logistics for camps, workshops, and parties, adapting programming in real time to different group dynamics, ability levels, and unexpected challenges while maintaining safety standards. These experiences taught me how to read the room, keep a group engaged, and create a warm, inclusive environment where participants feel safe to participate fully.

My work extends beyond the art studio into clinical and crisis contexts. I served as a Volunteer Crisis Counselor with The Trevor Project, providing culturally competent crisis support to LGBTQ+ youth, and I currently volunteer with Harmonia, where my training in crisis de-escalation, harm reduction, and trauma-informed care allows me to provide on-site emotional support to individuals experiencing acute psychological distress.

What draws me most to AWA is the belief that growth happens through connection, creativity, and kindness. I have seen firsthand how a safe space to create can open the door to emotional expression for young people who struggle to put their feelings into words. I would be honored to bring my experience in art facilitation, group management, and trauma-informed support to adolescents in your program, and I can offer consistent weekly or biweekly availability for on-site groups.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my creative practice and clinical training can contribute to your organization.

Warm regards,
Natalia Perez

Shamaiah Manriquez
South Florida
331-250-1652
ShamaiahM@Gmail.com

October 28, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in youth development, art instruction, creative education, and community programming, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an environment dedicated to supporting adolescents’ well-being, personal development, and growth.

My experience working with children and teens through the Boys & Girls Club and the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp has strengthened my appreciation for the importance of creating positive, structured, and encouraging environments where young people can develop confidence, explore their strengths, and express themselves constructively. Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

In 2025, I served as an art instructor for the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp, delivering structured art workshops for children and teenagers. I also led a community painting experience at JPP International Church through Painting With A Twist, facilitating an engaging group activity for approximately 40 participants. Earlier in my career, my work with the Boys & Girls Club involved youth art programming designed to encourage imagination, confidence, and self-expression. These experiences have reinforced my belief that young people benefit from opportunities to discover their abilities, develop positive relationships, and engage in activities that promote healthy self-expression.

I currently serve as Program Coordinator for Paint With Purpose, a community arts and creative wellness initiative that uses guided painting experiences to encourage self-expression, confidence, healing, and connection. My responsibilities include developing and coordinating creative workshops, planning activities, preparing materials, communicating with participants, and exploring partnerships with community organizations and schools. This work reflects my commitment to using creativity as a constructive way to bring people together and create meaningful community experiences.

In addition to my experience in youth programming and the arts, I bring more than 10 years of experience in administrative support, client relations, organizational coordination, and professional communication. My background includes supporting leadership, coordinating schedules and activities, managing documentation, and handling confidential information with discretion. These skills would allow me to contribute organization, reliability, professionalism, and effective communication to your team.

I am also pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at South Florida Bible College, with anticipated completion in 2028. My educational path complements my interest in human development, individual strengths, and the factors that contribute to personal growth and well-being. As an artist, published children’s book author, and creative educator, I am passionate about helping people recognize their potential and discover constructive ways to communicate and express themselves. My CPR and AED certification, obtained in 2023, further reflects my commitment to maintaining relevant practical skills.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, creativity, compassion, and organizational strengths to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to a supportive environment where adolescents are encouraged to develop healthy coping strategies, build confidence, strengthen interpersonal skills, and recognize their capacity for growth. I would be proud to contribute to a team that approaches youth development with professionalism, respect, consistency, and an understanding of the importance of individualized support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth development, creative programming, psychology studies, and professional administration could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its mission.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the clinical team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults, I bring a unique combination of clinical training, youth development, experiential education, and a genuine passion for helping young people navigate life's challenges.

My journey into clinical mental health counseling grew naturally from my years working in Jewish education, teen engagement, summer camps, and experiential programming. Throughout these experiences, I discovered that some of the most meaningful growth opportunities happen when young people feel connected, supported, and empowered to explore who they are. This philosophy continues to shape my work as a therapist today.

I earned my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and currently provide individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health. My clinical experience also includes working with adolescents at Family First and with young adults at New Directions for Young Adults, where I facilitated therapeutic groups focused on emotional regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, coping skills, and personal growth. These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

My clinical approach is grounded in Adlerian theory, with an emphasis on belonging, social connection, encouragement, and understanding the patterns that shape how individuals see themselves and the world. I integrate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions to create meaningful growth opportunities. I particularly enjoy incorporating creativity, active engagement, and play into the therapeutic process, recognizing that traditional talk therapy is not always the most effective way to connect with every adolescent.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to seeing beyond a teenager's presenting behaviors and recognizing the individual underneath. I strongly believe that adolescents deserve therapeutic spaces where they feel heard, respected, and valued, especially during some of their most challenging moments. Your collaborative, multidisciplinary treatment environment aligns with both my clinical philosophy and my longstanding commitment to supporting young people.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical skills, extensive experience in youth engagement, and enthusiasm for experiential therapeutic work to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and approach could contribute to the meaningful work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

In Community,

Ross Glinkenhouse, MS, Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a master's degree in counseling and professional experience in both child rehabilitation counseling and school counseling, I have developed a strong foundation in behavioral health, family engagement, client intake, and providing compassionate support to individuals navigating challenging circumstances. I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it would allow me to combine my counseling background with my passion for helping children, adolescents, and families access the care and resources they need.

In my previous role as a Child Rehabilitation Counselor at Keypoint Health Services, I worked closely with children experiencing emotional, behavioral, and mental health challenges, as well as their families. An important part of my responsibilities involved completing intakes with children and their families, gathering information about their needs, understanding their concerns, and helping determine appropriate services and support. These experiences taught me the importance of approaching each family with empathy, patience, and professionalism, especially when they are navigating difficult or overwhelming situations. I also conducted ongoing assessments, provided crisis intervention, connected families with community resources, and collaborated with families to support positive outcomes.

In my current role as an Elementary School Counselor with Baltimore County Public Schools, I continue to work closely with students and families to address social, emotional, behavioral, and academic needs. I regularly collaborate with parents, educators, and support teams to identify concerns, coordinate interventions, and connect families with appropriate resources. My experience has strengthened my ability to communicate effectively, build trusting relationships, manage sensitive information, and remain organized while balancing multiple responsibilities.

Additionally, my previous remote internship with 7 Cups of Tea provided me with experience supporting individuals through online communication, active listening, and collaborative problem-solving. I understand the importance of making individuals feel heard and supported, even when communication takes place virtually.

I believe my combination of behavioral health experience, direct intake experience, family engagement, and counseling education would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team. I would welcome the opportunity to be a reassuring first point of contact for individuals and families seeking treatment and to help make the admissions process as supportive and seamless as possible.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with your organization's needs.

Sincerely,
Kirsten Lyons

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. With a Bachelor’s degree in Health Services Management, a Master’s degree in Counseling and Human Services, and my Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) credential, I bring a strong educational and professional background in healthcare, counseling, communication, and supporting individuals during challenging times.

My background has strengthened my ability to communicate with compassion, listen without judgment, build rapport, and help individuals feel comfortable discussing sensitive concerns. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be overwhelming, especially for families navigating care for their adolescents. I believe every family deserves to feel heard, respected, supported, and guided through the admissions process with patience and understanding.

I also bring approximately two years of high-volume customer service experience with Faneuil, where I handled between 100 and 200 calls daily. This experience strengthened my ability to manage multiple conversations, address concerns, communicate effectively, maintain professionalism, and provide quality service in a fast-paced environment. I am comfortable working remotely, communicating by phone, documenting information accurately, and helping individuals navigate services and next steps.

I would welcome the opportunity to combine my counseling background, healthcare education, and communication skills to support adolescents and their families in accessing the care they need. I am passionate about making a meaningful difference and would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and experience can contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,
Tanya Randle, LPC

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

What drew me to the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position was the opportunity to be a reassuring first voice for someone who may not know where to begin. Reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be difficult enough. I would want that first conversation to feel welcoming, respectful, and free of judgement. 

My background in healthcare has taught me how much communication and follow through matter. At Option Care, I worked remotely managing insurance authorizations, coordinating with medical offices, and keeping track of important documentation and deadlines. Before that, I worked directly with patients at Spokane Obstetrics and Gynecology where I handled referrals, scheduling, and patient communication. I have learned how to navigate complicated processes while remembering that there is a real person on the other end.

Before entering healthcare, I spent several years caring for young children and supporting families. I also volunteered at Vanessa Behan Crisis Nursery, where I cared for young children while their parents navigated difficult circumstances. That experience taught me something I have carried ever since; you don't need to know someone's whole story to meet them with patience, understanding, and kindness. 

I am currently pursuing my degree in Psychology at USC Upstate, with the goal of building a career in mental health and advocacy. I know a kind voice won't always solve everything, but I do believe that it can make asking for help a little less intimidating. I would be absolutely grateful for the opportunity to bring my healthcare experience, compassion, and willingness to learn to your admissions team. 

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would genuinely appreciate the opportunity to connect.

Warmly, 

Ashley Howerton

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With more than eight years of experience across behavioral health, client support, and administrative services, I bring a strong combination of compassion, communication, and organizational skills that align well with this position.

In addition to my clinical experience, my previous role as a Call Center Representative with Genisys Credit Union strengthened my ability to manage high volumes of inbound calls, navigate sensitive conversations, resolve concerns, and maintain accurate records while working within established performance and confidentiality standards. I also bring administrative experience coordinating appointments, managing calendars, maintaining documentation, and communicating professionally with clients and colleagues.

I am currently pursuing my Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at Southern New Hampshire University with a concentration in Addiction Studies. My education has further strengthened my interest in behavioral health, substance use recovery, and the importance of accessible, compassionate treatment. I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it allows me to combine my professional experience with an area of study and a field I genuinely care about.

I understand that an admissions coordinator is often the first point of contact for someone seeking help, and that first interaction can make a meaningful difference. I would approach that responsibility with professionalism, empathy, attention to detail, and consistent follow-through. I am comfortable working independently in remote environments, managing competing priorities, and handling confidential information responsibly.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, education, and commitment to behavioral health could contribute to your admissions team. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,
Neely Shaelyn Kelley

November 21, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy / Principles Recovery Center

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With an Associate’s Degree in Medical Information Technology, a Hospital Admissions Specialist certification, and extensive experience in healthcare administration, health information management, patient support, and insurance processing, I believe my professional background aligns well with the responsibilities of this role.

During my time as a Health Information Specialist with Ciox Health, I developed expertise in managing confidential patient information, reviewing medical authorizations, ensuring HIPAA compliance, and maintaining accurate electronic health records. My responsibilities required careful attention to detail, independent decision-making, and the ability to consistently meet established productivity and quality standards while handling sensitive healthcare information.

My previous experience in clinical and pharmacy environments has further strengthened my patient communication and administrative skills. I have assisted physicians during patient examinations, documented clinical encounters, coordinated patient-related responsibilities, and processed prescription insurance claims. These experiences have given me a comprehensive understanding of healthcare operations and the importance of providing accurate, timely, and compassionate assistance to patients and their families.

Additionally, I have experience working with multiple electronic health record systems, including Cerner, MEDITECH, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, and HealthPort. I am highly adaptable, organized, and comfortable navigating healthcare technology while maintaining professionalism and confidentiality.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to make a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals and families seeking mental health and substance use treatment. I recognize that reaching out for help can be an incredibly vulnerable experience, and I believe the first interaction with a healthcare organization should provide reassurance, understanding, and a clear path forward. I would take pride in being a compassionate and dependable first point of contact for those seeking care.

I am confident that my healthcare experience, strong communication skills, attention to detail, and commitment to patient-centered service would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your organization’s mission of helping individuals and families access the treatment and support they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and dedication to quality patient care can contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Caitlin Patterson

Hello, 
My name is Megan Marsh.
While growing up I have always been in the field of helping others. When I was in high-school I stayed busy by being a camp counselor for youth and by being a teachers assistant for Kindergarten. I have always loved helping people and making people happy in any way that I could. 
When I graduated college with my associates degree, I went and worked a childcare center. There I worked with children from ages 6 weeks to school aged. I worked there for around 5 years until I decided to try something different. From there I started worked at a Applied Behaviorial Analysis clinic where I worked one on one with children on the spectrum. This sparked my love for behavior, data collection, and all why questions of why people behave the way we do. My time at the clinic pushed me into pursuing my Bachelor's degree in child and family studies. I completed my degree online while working full time and caring for my two children and all while keep a steady 3.5-4.0 GPA. I always thought that if I could do that than anyone could if they really wanted too. 
After completing my bachelor's degree I decided to try something out of my comfort zone to push me and help me grow. So, I accepted a position as a center manger of an early development center. This job has helped me grow in many ways personally and professionally but it does not make me feel fulfilled.
My dream job is to feel like I am making a difference and I want to help people. 
When I saw the description of this position I thought it could be what I am missing. 
With kind regards, 
Megan Marsh

Admissions Hiring Team

Dear Admissions Hiring Team,
A parent calling about a teenager may have spent days working up to the call and still be unsure
what to ask. An adult reaching out for help with substance use may have only a few private
minutes to talk. I’m applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position because I value what
a calm, attentive person can do in those first minutes: listen, answer the question the caller came
with, and make the next step clear.
As the primary contact for online graduate nursing programs at Liberty University, I helped
students figure out what stood between them and a practicum. I checked eligibility, explained
which documents were missing, and followed up. When a question involved another department, I
worked with that team to get the student an answer. Later, as Director of Clinical Operations, I
coordinated requirements for more than 600 nursing students. That work taught me to keep track
of individual details even when many people needed help at once.
Today I run a remote coaching practice, where I manage my own schedule, client communication,
and confidential records. Coaching has taught me to ask one question at a time and give people
room to answer. I would bring that habit, along with eight years of volunteer youth mentoring, to
conversations with the teens and families your academy serves and the adults who reach out to
Principles Recovery Center.
I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience with sensitive conversations, eligibility
review, and follow-up could serve your admissions team. Thank you for considering my
application.
Sincerely,
Nicole Horsch

candidates.cover_letter:
Melissa Johnson
Bostic, NC · mjjohns1194@gmail.com · 445-867-1424

Dear Hiring Team,

Your posting describes this role as "the first voice someone hears on their path to healing," and that sentence is exactly why I'm applying. I have done intake work in behavioral health, and I know what it means to be the person who answers when someone calls on one of the hardest days of their life. Meeting that call with compassion, and guiding the caller from that first conversation to a clear next step, is work I have done and work I believe in.

In 2023 I did intake work at Lower Merion Counseling Center, a Resources for Human Development program, where I was a first point of contact for individuals and families seeking treatment. I answered inbound calls, gathered the information needed to screen for fit, explained programs and next steps in plain, caring language, and coordinated the assessments, intake dates, and paperwork that got people through the door. Insurance verification was part of that role, and it is work I have done in other positions as well — I am comfortable confirming coverage and explaining, honestly and kindly, what it does and doesn't cover. I documented everything accurately in our systems, treated every caller's information with strict confidentiality, and followed up consistently so no one was left waiting without an answer. I also know this work from the other side of the phone, as someone who has navigated the healthcare system as a patient — it taught me exactly how much a calm, clear voice matters, and I have never forgotten it.

Alongside that, my years as a school photographer put me in front of hundreds of students and families on tight schedules. I worked with teenagers every day — including anxious, overwhelmed, and special-needs students — coordinated daily schedules across schools, and kept detailed records accurate under time pressure. Working in schools also meant strict expectations around student privacy, which I took seriously every day. That experience strengthened the same skills admissions runs on: a warm and confident phone presence, patience with people in distress, and follow-through until every person is scheduled or pointed to the right place.

I am highly organized and self-directed, comfortable managing my own pipeline of calls and follow-ups without daily direction, and accurate with CRM and EMR documentation. I would welcome the chance to put direct behavioral health intake experience to work for the families calling Adolescent Wellness Academy and the clients calling Principles Recovery Center.

Thank you for your consideration. I would be glad to speak with you about how my experience could serve your admissions team.

Warmly,
Melissa Johnson

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. After reading your job description, I felt this was an opportunity that closely aligns with both my professional background and my personal experiences.

I bring a unique combination of healthcare experience and firsthand understanding of addiction and mental health. I grew up witnessing my mother's struggles with active addiction, and I have been in recovery myself for over 20 years. I have also experienced the mental health challenges that can accompany addiction, both personally and within my own family. As a parent of a child who has faced mental health challenges, I understand how overwhelming, frightening, and isolating it can be for families trying to find the right help for someone they love.

These experiences have given me a genuine understanding of the importance of that first conversation. When someone reaches out for help, they may be scared, uncertain, embarrassed, or simply not know where to turn. I understand how much it matters to be met with compassion, patience, and someone willing to listen without judgment. I would take great pride in being that first reassuring voice for individuals and families during some of their most difficult moments.

Professionally, I bring experience in healthcare administration, patient admissions, insurance verification, and prior authorizations. My previous healthcare roles have given me experience navigating insurance requirements, communicating with patients and healthcare providers, handling sensitive information, and coordinating the administrative steps necessary to access care. I also have a background as a CNA, which has given me valuable firsthand experience in patient care and an appreciation for the importance of treating every individual with dignity and respect.

I believe my professional knowledge, combined with my personal perspective, would allow me to connect with callers in a meaningful way while confidently managing the administrative responsibilities of this position. I understand that this role requires more than answering phones. It requires follow-through, organization, empathy, and the ability to help people navigate what can often feel like an overwhelming process.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, and dedication to your team. Most importantly, I would love to be part of an organization that helps individuals and families find a path toward healing and a better future.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.

Sincerely,

Heather Nelson

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With more than 10 years of experience in customer service, administrative coordination, healthcare support, and remote operations, I bring a combination of compassion, organization, and strong communication skills that I believe would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Throughout my career, I have worked in roles requiring professionalism, sensitivity, and the ability to build trust with individuals from a variety of backgrounds. My experience as a Personal Care Assistant with Our Hospice of South Central Indiana strengthened my ability to approach individuals and families with empathy, patience, and understanding during some of life's most difficult moments. I understand the importance of making people feel heard, respected, and supported, particularly when they are navigating unfamiliar or challenging circumstances.

In my previous remote position as a Sales Coordinator with Plug Power, I managed a high volume of communications, coordinated complex processes, maintained accurate records, and ensured consistent follow-through with both internal teams and external customers. I am comfortable working independently, managing competing priorities, learning new systems, and taking ownership of responsibilities without requiring constant direction.

What particularly appeals to me about this opportunity is the chance to combine my administrative and coordination experience with meaningful work that can positively impact individuals and families. I recognize that an initial admissions call can be an important first step toward receiving help, and I would take that responsibility seriously by providing a welcoming, professional, and compassionate experience to every caller.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare experience, remote work background, attention to detail, and commitment to helping others to your organization. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and strengths could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,  
Amanda Hardin

Of all the roles I’ve held in healthcare, my favorite was serving as an ITP Administrator at Advantage Behavioral Health Services. That’s why I’m applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Before we hang up, I want them to know what the next step is, who will reach out, and when they can expect to hear back.

I bring nearly 12 years of healthcare administration experience, including behavioral health documentation, patient scheduling, and insurance verification. Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With experience in healthcare customer service, patient support, and administrative responsibilities, I believe I could bring strong communication, organization, and compassion to your team.

In my previous role with a durable medical equipment company, I worked in a call center assisting patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers with equipment orders, deliveries, insurance-related questions, and other concerns. I used Brightree to access and update patient information, maintain accurate records, and help ensure requests were handled efficiently. This experience taught me the importance of patience, confidentiality, attention to detail, and treating every caller with understanding and respect.

I am comfortable handling a high volume of calls, communicating with people who may be frustrated or overwhelmed, and following through to make sure their needs are addressed. I also have experience in office support and customer service, which has helped me develop strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple responsibilities.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because of the chance to help individuals and families take an important first step toward receiving mental health and substance use treatment. I understand how important that initial interaction can be, and I would take pride in making callers feel heard, supported, and informed throughout the admissions process.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my healthcare customer service experience and skills could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Alexsia D’Arcy

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my communication skills, work ethic, and ability to connect with people to your team. I am looking for a position where I can grow professionally while doing work that has a meaningful purpose, and this opportunity feels like a particularly good fit for that.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would love the opportunity to speak with you further about how I could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Eloise Carter

Tierra Ennis

November 21, 2026

Adolescent Wellness Academy

Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. My background in healthcare coordination and patient intake has given me valuable experience supporting individuals who need access to essential services. I understand how important the first conversation can be for someone seeking mental health treatment. I would welcome the opportunity to help adolescents and their families feel supported throughout the admissions process.

In my current role at Carenet Healthcare, I provide Enhanced Care Management (ECM) support and screen members for mental health referrals. I also coordinate access to housing assistance and food assistance programs. My responsibilities include creating and billing patient intakes, reviewing insurance eligibility, verifying medical necessity, and coordinating documentation with healthcare providers. I regularly review medical records and diagnosis codes to ensure accuracy and compliance with program requirements.

My experience has taught me how to guide individuals through sensitive conversations with patience and professionalism. I understand the importance of explaining services clearly and helping members understand their next steps. I am comfortable managing multiple cases while maintaining accurate records and protecting confidential health information. I also understand that consistent follow-up is essential to helping people receive the care they need.

In addition to my healthcare experience, I bring a strong background in customer service and administrative coordination. I have extensive experience communicating by phone and email while managing documentation and resolving outstanding requests. My remote work experience has strengthened my ability to stay organized and work independently without sacrificing quality.

What interests me most about Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to make a meaningful difference during a vulnerable time in someone’s life. I recognize that reaching out for mental health support can be difficult for both adolescents and their families. I would take pride in being a compassionate and dependable first point of contact who helps make that process less overwhelming.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my healthcare intake experience and commitment to patient-centered service align with your team’s needs. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,
Tierra Ennis

Christina McHaffie
Clinton, Missouri
November 20, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Principles Recovery Center

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. My professional background includes healthcare support, therapeutic foster care, business ownership, and coordinating services for individuals with complex medical, developmental, and behavioral needs. I believe these experiences have prepared me to provide the compassionate communication, organization, and dependable follow-through essential to your admissions team.

Throughout my years as a therapeutic foster parent, I supported children and adolescents facing significant emotional, behavioral, and developmental challenges. I regularly coordinated medical appointments, counseling services, educational needs, and communication between families, healthcare professionals, and community agencies. This experience taught me the importance of listening without judgment, maintaining confidentiality, and helping families navigate unfamiliar and often overwhelming situations.

My additional experience as a chiropractic assistant and owner of Hands for Health Massage strengthened my abilities in client communication, scheduling, documentation, bookkeeping, and independently managing daily responsibilities. More recently, my work in self-directed support services has further developed my skills in coordinating care, maintaining accurate records, and advocating for individuals with complex needs.

I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an incredibly difficult first step. I would welcome the opportunity to help individuals and families feel heard, respected, and supported while connecting them with appropriate services.

I am organized, dependable, comfortable working independently, and committed to learning the systems and procedures necessary to succeed in this role.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and dedication to helping others could benefit your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Christina McHaffie

Amber Loggins
Loganville, GA · 678-724-1485 · ambermoongreene@gmail.com
November 21, 2026
Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy
Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment
Dear Hiring Team,
When a parent reaches out about a teenager who is struggling, that first conversation matters. They are often scared, overwhelmed, and unsure what happens next. For the past year and a half, I have been the person on the other end of that call, guiding families through behavioral health admissions with patience, clear answers, and steady follow-through. I would love to bring that experience to Adolescent Wellness Academy as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator.
As an Admissions Coordinator at Flyland Recovery Network, and before that at a behavioral health organization in West Palm Beach, I managed inbound inquiries, screened client needs, verified insurance, completed intake paperwork, and coordinated transportation and arrival logistics. I guided each case from first contact through admission, kept families informed at every step, and handled sensitive conversations with care and discretion. In my current role as Patient Care Coordinator, I coordinate appointments, referrals, aftercare, and documentation across teams, so I also understand what happens after admission and why accurate intake work sets a patient up for success.
What I would bring to your team:
• Admissions experience in mental health and substance use treatment: inquiry handling, screening, insurance verification, and intake
• Family-centered communication: calm, compassionate, and clear when the stakes are high
• Accuracy and organization: CRM and EMR data entry, thorough documentation, and timely follow-up on every open case
• Remote-ready work habits: comfortable managing a full caseload by phone, email, and virtual collaboration tools
Earlier roles in patient scheduling, banking, and high-volume inside sales strengthened my ability to juggle competing priorities without losing the personal touch. I am also completing an Associate of Science at Southern New Hampshire University with a 3.889 GPA, which reflects the same consistency I bring to my work.
I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can help families take the first step toward care. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Amber Loggins

candidates.cover_letter:
Hi!

I’m applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. I have a background in EMS, medical office work, and administrative work, and I think my experience makes me a good fit for this role.

Working as an EMT taught me a lot about dealing with people during some of the hardest moments of their lives. I’ve learned how important it is to stay calm, listen, and treat people with kindness and understanding, especially when they’re scared or overwhelmed.

This position also means a little more to me on a personal level. I had only been working my first EMS job for a couple of weeks when my brother had his first overdose. Over the next several years, I watched him struggle with addiction and personally had to administer Narcan to him twice before eventually losing him to an overdose. So, I know firsthand what it’s like to be the family member on the other side, feeling scared, helpless, and not knowing what to do next. I know how much it can mean to have someone who genuinely cares and is willing to help.

On the work side of things, I also have experience with insurance verification, prior authorizations, patient records, and other administrative tasks. I’m comfortable working on my own, keeping things organized, and learning new systems.

I feel like this position would give me the opportunity to use both my work experience and my personal experiences to help people who are going through some really difficult situations. I’d love to be able to make that process a little less overwhelming for someone.

Thank you for considering my application!

Heather Lewis

Desiree Brown
Alexandria, Louisiana
[Your Phone Number] | [Your Professional Email]

November 20, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am deeply passionate about the opportunity to join Adolescent Wellness Academy as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator. Professionally, I bring over six years of experience in the mental health field. Personally, I bring nearly 20 years of life experiences shaped by supporting family members and friends throughout their mental health journeys. These experiences have continually taught me the importance of understanding others beyond their immediate circumstances. Patience, calmness, and empathy are qualities that come naturally to me. Combined with my warm and engaging personality, they allow me to create meaningful connections and provide reassurance, even through a simple phone conversation.

During my time at Woodland Springs Behavioral Health, I began my career as a Behavioral Health Technician (BHT) working mainly on the Adolescent units,before advancing into an Intake Coordinator position. This transition allowed me to experience two equally important aspects of patient care: building relationships with patients during treatment and supporting individuals and families as they entered or completed the admissions process. Witnessing patients arrive during some of their most vulnerable moments and later recognizing their progress strengthened my appreciation for the trust placed in behavioral health professionals.

My experience has also taught me that compassion is especially important when working with individuals who may be frightened, frustrated, or resistant to treatment. I understand that anger and resistance can sometimes mask fear, uncertainty, or emotional distress. Rather than focusing solely on someone’s immediate reaction, I strive to understand the person behind the behavior, establish trust, and create an environment where individuals feel safe enough to communicate openly. I recognize that seeking treatment can be intimidating, and I believe meaningful support begins with making people feel heard rather than judged.

As an Intake Coordinator, I managed incoming admissions calls, conducted patient intake assessments, verified insurance coverage and benefits, and coordinated admissions with nurses, physicians, and other healthcare professionals. I also maintained accurate patient records and guided families through the admissions process. These responsibilities strengthened my ability to navigate sensitive situations with professionalism, organization, empathy, and attention to detail.

I understand how overwhelming seeking mental health or substance use treatment can be for families, particularly when their children are involved. My professional background, combined with my personal understanding of mental health challenges, has prepared me to approach these conversations with compassion, patience, and reassurance.

For me, working in mental health is more than a profession; it is an extension of who I am. I would be honored to bring my experience, dedication, and genuine care for others to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for considering my application. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Desiree Brown

# Cover Letter
**Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment**

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With experience in healthcare administration, patient scheduling, records management, dispatching, and customer service, I bring strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills that I believe would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Throughout my previous roles, I have developed the ability to manage multiple responsibilities, communicate professionally with individuals from diverse backgrounds, maintain accurate records, and handle sensitive information with discretion. My healthcare-related experience has strengthened my understanding of the importance of compassion, patience, confidentiality, and attention to detail when working with individuals navigating challenging circumstances.

On a personal level, mental health is something I deeply understand. In 2018, I was diagnosed with anxiety and psychosis, which gave me firsthand experience with mental health challenges and the importance of understanding, compassion, and access to appropriate support. My personal experiences have helped me develop a deeper appreciation for what individuals and families may go through when seeking mental health care. I believe this perspective would allow me to approach families with genuine empathy, patience, and without judgment.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to combine my administrative and healthcare experience with meaningful work that helps adolescents and their families access the support and treatment they need. I understand that the admissions process can be overwhelming for families, and I would approach every interaction with empathy, professionalism, and a genuine desire to make the process as smooth and welcoming as possible.

I am dependable, adaptable, detail-oriented, and comfortable learning new systems and technology. I take pride in being someone others can rely on, communicating effectively, and ensuring that important details are never overlooked. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my professional skills and personal understanding to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, work ethic, and dedication to helping others could benefit your organization.

Sincerely,  
Makayla

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Admissions position with your organization. With nearly six years of experience at Action Behavior Centers, including extensive experience in behavioral health admissions, client intake, scheduling, and family communication, I believe my background aligns closely with the responsibilities of this role.

In my current position as a Clinic Admissions Associate, I work remotely and independently manage admissions processes, communicate with families and healthcare providers, coordinate initial assessments, obtain necessary documentation, and guide families through each step of beginning services. I am experienced in handling sensitive information, maintaining HIPAA compliance, managing multiple priorities, and ensuring families receive timely and compassionate support.

My experience has also allowed me to develop strong communication, organizational, and problem solving skills. I understand that families seeking behavioral health services are often navigating stressful and emotional situations, and I take pride in providing a welcoming, supportive, and professional experience from their very first interaction.

Having successfully worked in a remote environment, I am comfortable managing my own workload, maintaining consistent follow through, and collaborating with team members virtually. I am confident that my admissions background, dedication to client care, and ability to work independently would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your team.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills align with your organization’s needs. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,
Jessica Garvin

Sincerely,

Maribel Conde Colón

Diego Mattison-Santos
Fort Pierce, FL 34946

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Case Manager position with your organization. As a recent graduate of Florida Atlantic University with a Bachelor of Social Work degree and professional experience working as a Case Manager at PUR Health and Wellness, I am confident that my education, experience, and passion for helping others would make me a valuable addition to your team.

During my time at PUR Health and Wellness, I gained hands-on experience assessing client needs, developing individualized goals, connecting individuals with community resources, and coordinating services related to housing, employment, and education. I also assisted with outside care coordination, family communication, and discharge planning to help ensure clients had appropriate support when transitioning to another level of care. Additionally, I gained experience using Kipu for documentation and client-related case management responsibilities.

My previous experience as a Case Manager BSW with Criminal Conflict and Civil Regional further strengthened my ability to conduct client check-ins, document interactions, complete community referrals, and apply confidentiality and trauma-informed practices. Through my experience as a Help Line Student Support Specialist at Florida Atlantic University, I also developed strong communication skills while providing support and resources to students experiencing challenging circumstances.

My background has taught me the importance of meeting clients where they are, recognizing their individual strengths, advocating for their needs, and helping them work toward greater stability and independence. I am committed to providing compassionate, professional, and client-centered services while maintaining ethical standards and confidentiality.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my case management experience, social work education, and dedication to serving individuals and families to your organization. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss my qualifications further.

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I’m excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. Caring for others has always been the part of my work that means the most to me. Recent changes in my life mean I need to work remotely, and I felt discouraged when I realized I would have to step away from hands-on caregiving. When I came across your listing, I felt excited about what I could do next. It felt like the best of both worlds. I could work from home and still spend my days doing something I care deeply about, helping people feel supported when they need it most.

My experience in caregiving, running an in-home daycare, and customer service has taught me how to listen closely, stay calm when someone is overwhelmed, and explain next steps clearly. Caring for adults with traumatic brain injuries taught me the importance of patience and dignity. Running a daycare taught me how much families value someone who takes their concerns seriously and follows through on what they say they’ll do.

What draws me most to this role is the chance to be one of the first people a family speaks with when they’re seeking mental health or substance use treatment for their teen. I would want every family I speak with to feel comfortable asking questions, know that their concerns were heard, and leave the conversation with a clear understanding of what comes next.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to bring my caregiving and customer service experience to your admissions team and help families take that first step toward care.

Sincerely,
Katelyn Mayes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am reaching out because I am genuinely interested in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I actually applied for this position before and unfortunately wasn’t selected. But when I saw the opportunity again, I knew I wanted to try one more time because I truly believe this is the kind of work I am meant to do.

I currently work as a House Manager at ADH Recovery, and before that I worked as a Behavioral Health Technician at Rays of Sonshine. I have hands-on experience with admissions, intake, documentation, medication monitoring, and helping people navigate some of the most difficult moments of their lives. I am also familiar with Kipu and understand how important accuracy, communication, and compassion are in a treatment setting.

What makes this position so meaningful to me is knowing that when someone reaches out for treatment, they may be making one of the hardest decisions of their life. That first conversation matters. The person on the other end of the phone has the opportunity to make someone feel safe, understood, and hopeful. That’s something I would never take lightly.

I’m currently attending Southern New Hampshire University, working toward my bachelor’s degree in Psychology with a focus on addiction. I’m continuing my education because this field isn’t just a temporary career choice for me. It’s something I care deeply about, and I want to continue learning and growing.

I understand that I wasn’t selected the first time I applied, and I respect that decision. But I hope you’ll consider giving my application another look. I know I still have things to learn, but I am dependable, compassionate, hardworking, and willing to put in the effort to become a valuable part of your team.

I’m not asking to be given a position I haven’t earned. I’m simply hoping for the chance to interview and show you what I have to offer. I believe my experience, dedication, and genuine passion for helping people would make me a strong addition to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Thank you for considering me again. Regardless of the outcome, I appreciate the work your organization does for individuals and families who need support.

Sincerely,

Ashley Tucker

Dr. Kristina Berrios, MSW, DSW

Dear Hiring Committee,
I am writing to express my interest in the Instructor Pool position within Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies for the 2026–2027 academic year. With a Doctor of Social Work from Simmons University, a strong background in social justice, and extensive experience in leadership, professional development, and human services, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an inclusive and engaging academic environment.
Throughout my professional and academic career, I have developed a deep understanding of intersectionality, systemic oppression, identity, social inequities, and the impact of institutional structures on historically marginalized populations. My doctoral research focused on culturally responsive practices, equity, implicit bias, and addressing systemic disparities affecting African American youth within the foster care system.
Since 2022, I have served as a Master of Social Work field instructor, supporting students in connecting academic theories to professional practice, developing critical thinking skills, and strengthening their professional identities. My experience also includes curriculum development, instructional design, staff training, mentorship, and program evaluation.
My teaching philosophy is centered on creating an inclusive learning environment where students feel comfortable asking questions, examining diverse perspectives, and engaging in meaningful discussions. I believe education should encourage students to think critically about their own experiences, challenge assumptions, and explore how gender, race, sexuality, socioeconomic status, and other social identities intersect to shape individual and collective experiences.
As an educator and social work professional, I bring both academic knowledge and practical experience to the classroom. I am particularly interested in helping students understand the connections between theory, lived experiences, social policy, power, privilege, and advocacy.
I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my knowledge, professional experience, and passion for education to the Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies program. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and teaching philosophy align with the department's academic goals.
Sincerely,
Dr. Kristina Berrios, MSW, DSW

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in an employment opportunity with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in behavioral health and a strong passion for supporting children, adolescents, and families, I believe my background and dedication would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current position as a Behavioral Specialist with Behavioral Specialists of Louisiana, I provide individualized support to children with Autism Spectrum Disorder, developmental disabilities, and behavioral challenges.
