candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With approximately 10 years of experience in coordination, client communication, intake, referral management, and relationship-building, I bring a strong background in helping people navigate unfamiliar and sometimes emotionally challenging situations with compassion, patience, and professionalism.

Throughout my career in animal welfare, I have worked extensively with individuals and families navigating difficult circumstances, often serving as their first point of contact during stressful and time-sensitive situations. My experience has required me to listen carefully, identify individual needs, communicate available options, coordinate appropriate next steps, and maintain consistent follow-through. I understand the importance of making people feel heard rather than making them feel like another name on a spreadsheet.

In my previous role as Volunteer Coordinator with the Humane Society of Washington County, I managed a growing volunteer program, increasing monthly volunteer participation from 56 to more than 260 individuals. This required substantial independent organization, ongoing communication, onboarding, scheduling, recordkeeping, and coordination across multiple departments. My earlier experience coordinating offsite adoptions also involved managing a high volume of inquiries, facilitating referrals, assessing individual circumstances, and helping people navigate the process from initial contact through completion.

In my current coordination role with the Frederick County Health Department, I communicate directly with schools and healthcare personnel to coordinate hearing and vision screening services. This work requires attention to detail, proactive communication, accurate information gathering, and the ability to manage multiple moving pieces while ensuring appointments and logistical requirements are handled. 

I would love to bring those skills into a setting where compassionate communication can make a meaningful difference in someone’s life. I recognize that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable experience, particularly for adolescents and their families. I would approach every interaction with empathy, discretion, and respect, understanding that the first conversation can play an important role in someone’s willingness to pursue care.

I am comfortable learning new technology, managing competing priorities, maintaining organized records, and taking ownership of responsibilities with minimal supervision. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my coordination experience, strong communication skills, and commitment to compassionate service to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and approach to client support could contribute to your programs.

Sincerely,

Brittney Mair

candidates.cover_letter:
Cover Letter – Admissions Coordinator | Adolescent Recovery & Mental Health

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Admissions Coordinator position within your adolescent recovery and mental health program. With more than four years of experience in rehabilitation settings specializing in substance abuse, addiction recovery, and mental health, along with experience as a Care Coordinator and Case Manager, I bring a well-rounded understanding of the treatment process, the importance of effective care coordination, and the impact compassionate support can have on an individual’s recovery.

My experience in behavioral health has taught me that entering treatment can be one of the most vulnerable and overwhelming moments for an individual and their family. My understanding of mental health is also personal. Having experienced struggles with my own mental health, I understand how difficult, confusing, and intimidating it can be to recognize that something isn’t right and to reach the point of needing help. That perspective has given me a deeper sense of empathy for individuals who may feel scared, uncertain, misunderstood, or vulnerable, particularly adolescents who are still learning how to understand and navigate their emotions and mental health. I believe the way someone is met during that moment can make a lasting difference in whether they feel safe enough to accept support.

In my role as a Care Coordinator and Case Manager, I gained firsthand experience in coordinating care, supporting treatment plans, and helping ensure individuals had appropriate resources and continuity of care upon discharge. I understand that successful treatment extends beyond the walls of a facility, and that the right support, planning, and connections can make a meaningful difference in someone’s long-term recovery. This perspective allows me to recognize the importance of admissions not simply as an administrative process, but as the beginning of a critical opportunity to connect someone with the care they need.

I would bring to your team a strong foundation in rehabilitation and behavioral health, the ability to communicate effectively with individuals and families during difficult situations, attention to detail, and a genuine commitment to making a difference. I am particularly drawn to working with adolescents because I believe early access to treatment, consistent support, and a compassionate therapeutic environment can change the trajectory of a young person’s life. No adolescent should feel ashamed or alone for struggling, and I would strive to help every individual and family feel heard, respected, and supported from their very first interaction.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, dedication, and personal understanding of mental health to your admissions team. Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how I could contribute to your program and the individuals and families you serve.

Sincerely,
Joan masallo

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a professional background as a Residential Services Director and extensive experience supporting individuals navigating complex mental health, substance use, and crisis-related challenges, I believe I bring the compassion, leadership, communication skills, and dedication necessary to make a meaningful contribution to your team.

In my previous role as a Residential Services Director, I had the responsibility of running a domestic violence and sexual assault emergency shelter, working with individuals experiencing significant life challenges, including co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders. This experience strengthened my ability to connect with people from all walks of life, approach sensitive situations with empathy and understanding, and provide support during some of the most difficult moments in their lives.

My experience also includes crisis line response, scheduling, coordinating services, communicating with individuals in distress, and helping people navigate available resources and support systems. I understand that the first interaction someone has with a treatment facility can be incredibly important. It takes patience, compassion, professionalism, and the ability to make people feel heard, respected, and comfortable enough to take that first step toward receiving help.

I consider myself a natural people person who is approachable, easy to talk to, and genuinely passionate about helping others. I am equally comfortable managing administrative responsibilities and handling emotionally sensitive conversations. I understand the importance of being organized, responsive, dependable, and attentive to detail, particularly in an admissions setting where timely communication and coordination can make a significant difference.

What particularly interests me about Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to help adolescents and their families navigate the process of accessing mental health and substance use treatment. I recognize that reaching out for help can be overwhelming for both young people and their families. I would welcome the opportunity to be a reassuring, compassionate, and knowledgeable first point of contact during that process.

I would be proud to bring my leadership experience, crisis intervention background, interpersonal strengths, and genuine passion for helping others to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with your team's needs.

Sincerely,

Tabatha Hunt

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. As a psychology graduate from Portland State University's University Honors College, where I graduated summa cum laude with a 3.96 GPA, I am drawn to the opportunity to help individuals and families navigate the first steps toward mental health and substance use treatment. I value the importance of making people feel heard, respected, and supported, particularly when they are reaching out during difficult or uncertain moments.

My academic and professional experiences have strengthened the communication, organization, and interpersonal skills essential to this role. As an honors thesis researcher, I designed and conducted IRB-approved semi-structured interviews with seven undergraduate participants about sensitive bereavement experiences. This work required establishing rapport, listening without judgment, communicating thoughtfully, maintaining accurate documentation, and following established ethical and confidentiality requirements. I also analyzed participant responses and communicated findings with care and objectivity. These experiences reinforced the importance of approaching sensitive conversations with empathy, professionalism, and respect for individual circumstances.

My customer service experience at Fred Meyer and Safeway further developed my ability to communicate effectively, respond to inquiries, resolve concerns, and coordinate customer needs. At Fred Meyer, I regularly communicated with customers by phone regarding order updates, substitutions, and pickup scheduling while maintaining accurate transaction records and managing competing responsibilities. Additionally, my experience volunteering at a senior center involved providing individualized support, building rapport, facilitating activities, and communicating relevant observations about participants' well-being to staff.

I also want to be transparent that my background has not yet included a formal behavioral health admissions position or a dedicated remote admissions role. While I may not bring direct experience with every aspect of your admissions process, I bring a strong academic foundation in psychology, relevant experience communicating about sensitive topics, and a demonstrated ability to learn, adapt, and take responsibility for detailed work. I am highly trainable, receptive to feedback, and committed to developing the knowledge and technical skills necessary to perform the role successfully. I would welcome the opportunity to learn your specific admissions procedures, PHP and IOP program requirements, insurance verification processes, and CRM and EMR systems.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because of its focus on connecting individuals and families with appropriate behavioral health services. My academic background includes coursework in abnormal psychology, psychopathology, human development, counseling, and death, dying, and bereavement. I am also pursuing graduate-level education in clinical mental health counseling, reflecting my long-term commitment to the behavioral health field. I understand that the admissions process is more than scheduling an appointment; it is often a person's first interaction with a treatment program, and that interaction can influence whether they feel comfortable taking the next step.

I would bring strong written and verbal communication, active listening, attention to detail, sound judgment, adaptability, and a genuine commitment to compassionate service. I am eager to grow professionally, take initiative, and become a dependable member of your admissions team. I would appreciate the opportunity to demonstrate my capabilities and learn the processes necessary to contribute meaningfully to your programs.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education, transferable experience, and willingness to learn could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,

Rakhi Grey

Kimberly Mitchell
423-312-8409



November 20, 2026

Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Admissions Team,

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in residential facility management, youth advocacy, and high-volume client intake and coordination, I bring a trauma-informed, organized, and compassionate approach to guiding adolescents and their families through the admissions process.

Navigating behavioral health admissions is often an overwhelming and emotional milestone for families and young people. In my previous role as House Manager at MATS Shelter in Morristown, TN, I directly oversaw daily facility operations, resident intake procedures, safety compliance, and crisis de-escalation in a residential environment. That experience taught me how to balance empathetic, person-centered support with strict adherence to facility protocols, accurate record-keeping, and seamless coordination among clinical, residential, and administrative teams.

Additionally, my professional background collaborating with youth-serving agencies—including the Jacksonville Children's Commission, the Department of Juvenile Justice, and The Bridge of Northeast Florida—has given me a deep understanding of juvenile care systems, community resources, and inter-agency referral workflows. Whether communicating with families, probation officers, social workers, or clinical staff, I know how to gather critical intake information efficiently while maintaining confidentiality and building immediate rapport.

In the Admissions Coordinator role at Adolescent Wellness Academy, I will contribute:

* End-to-End Intake & Residential Operations: Proven ability to manage admissions screenings, verify documentation, coordinate bed availability, and ensure smooth, welcoming transitions into care.
* Youth & Family Engagement: A calm, reassuring presence when speaking with adolescents and caregivers in crisis, rooted in active listening and clear, transparent communication.
* Inter-Agency & Clinical Collaboration: Established familiarity working alongside juvenile justice, child welfare, and community behavioral health partners to align care plans and referral requirements.
* Administrative Precision: Strong organizational skills in maintaining compliant intake records, scheduling assessments, and tracking admissions pipelines under tight timelines.

I have professional references from my work with the Jacksonville Children's Commission, the Department of Juvenile Justice, and The Bridge of Northeast Florida who can speak directly to my integrity, work ethic, and dedication to youth services.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my residential leadership experience and background in youth and family coordination can support the admissions team at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Kimberly Mitchell

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. Throughout my career, I have discovered that what motivates me most is the opportunity to make a positive impact on others, whether through providing support, helping someone recognize their potential, or contributing to an environment where people can grow and succeed. I would welcome the opportunity to bring that same dedication and enthusiasm to your team.

My professional journey began onsite in Twin Falls with Universal American as a Customer Service Associate. Within just two months of taking calls, I became the fastest person working for Everise to be promoted to the escalation team for our line of business. Over time, I expanded my responsibilities to include a larger variety of calls, assisting as a subject matter expert to other CSAs, and developed a strong understanding of the importance of effective communication, patience, and finding solutions.

After 3 years of providing excellent service to customers, I was promoted to Supervisor. In that position, I had the opportunity to help team members develop their skills and advance in their careers. I also learned the importance of balancing empathy and understanding with accountability and organizational expectations. Supporting agents through sensitive and sometimes emotional conversations required patience, active listening, professionalism, and the ability to provide guidance without losing sight of the standards we were expected to maintain.

While I appreciated the leadership experience, I realized that my greatest professional fulfillment came from quality-focused work and helping others improve. This realization led me to pursue a Quality Assurance position with a newly established line of business supporting Illinois Meridian Medicaid.

Over the past five years in Quality Assurance, I have continued to grow alongside an expanding organization, taking on additional responsibilities and supporting multiple lines of business across various states. Throughout these changes, I have consistently maintained performance with little to no variance from client expectations. My ability to adapt quickly, learn new processes, and embrace changing responsibilities has been instrumental in my continued success.

While my background has primarily been in healthcare customer service, leadership, and quality assurance, I believe the skills I have developed translate meaningfully to the Admissions Coordinator position. I bring experience navigating sensitive conversations, supporting individuals through challenging situations, communicating expectations with compassion, maintaining accurate documentation, and recognizing opportunities for improvement. I understand that even when a conversation involves difficult circumstances, people deserve to feel heard, respected, and treated with dignity.

What particularly interests me about Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to contribute to something that reaches beyond the workplace. I want to be part of an organization that helps adolescents and families navigate challenging circumstances and creates opportunities for positive change. The possibility of playing even a small part in helping young people access the support and resources they need is something I find genuinely meaningful.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my adaptability, eagerness to learn, attention to quality, and passion for helping others to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am excited by the possibility of growing with your organization while contributing to work that makes a lasting difference in people's lives.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, strengths, and enthusiasm could contribute to your team.

Warm regards,

Kristina Stevens

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Mental Health Crisis Support position. While I may not have the traditional professional experience or background that some candidates bring to this role, I believe I have something equally important: genuine empathy, compassion, patience, and a deep understanding of how difficult life can become when someone feels like they have nowhere to turn.

My teenage years were incredibly difficult, and I faced personal struggles that challenged me in ways I never imagined. Those experiences gave me a different perspective on pain, hardship, and the importance of having someone who genuinely listens without judgment. I understand what it can feel like to be overwhelmed, lost, unheard, or unsure of how to move forward. I also understand how much of a difference one compassionate person can make during someone's darkest moments.

I believe I have the personality and emotional understanding needed to help people through some of the toughest battles of their lives. I am naturally empathetic, a good listener, and someone who wants others to feel seen, heard, and valued. I would approach every individual with kindness, respect, patience, and an open mind, understanding that everyone's circumstances and struggles are different.

I recognize that crisis support requires more than a caring personality. It requires professionalism, strong communication skills, appropriate boundaries, sound judgment, and a willingness to learn the proper training and procedures to support people safely and effectively. I would welcome the opportunity to develop those skills and grow within this field.

More than anything, I want to pursue work that has a meaningful impact on someone's life. If I can help someone feel a little less alone, remind them that their life matters, or help them find hope when things feel impossible, then I would consider that work incredibly meaningful.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my compassion, life experience, willingness to learn, and dedication to your team. I hope to have the opportunity to demonstrate that sometimes the ability to understand people comes not only from professional experience but also from the challenges we have overcome ourselves.

**Sincerely,**
Megan

One thing I want you to remember: Don't discount yourself because your experience doesn't look like everyone else's. Your lived experience can give you a valuable perspective, and your willingness to learn the professional skills needed to support people safely is just as important.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I am drawn to this opportunity because it allows me to combine strong communication skills, compassion, organization, and a genuine desire to help people during some of the most difficult moments of their lives.

I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can feel overwhelming, both for individuals and for their families. I believe the first interaction can make a meaningful difference in helping someone feel heard, supported, and comfortable taking the next step toward recovery. I would approach every call with patience, empathy, professionalism, and respect, while ensuring callers receive clear information and guidance.

I am confident in my ability to manage multiple inquiries, maintain accurate documentation, follow up consistently, and coordinate the steps necessary to help individuals move forward with care. I understand the importance of confidentiality, attention to detail, timely communication, and treating every person with dignity. I am also comfortable working independently in a remote environment while remaining accountable, organized, and focused on meeting goals.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your admissions team and help make the process of accessing treatment as supportive and seamless as possible for clients, families, and referral partners. I am especially inspired by your mission of helping adolescents and adults find the care and support they need to begin healing.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my skills, dedication, and compassionate approach could make me a valuable addition to your team.

Sincerely,
Dianne Dookie

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Intake Crisis Coordinator position. With approximately six years of experience working in healthcare, particularly in dementia and memory care, I have developed a strong foundation in compassionate communication, behavioral observation, crisis response, and supporting vulnerable individuals through difficult and often unpredictable circumstances.

Throughout my healthcare career, I have worked closely with individuals experiencing cognitive impairment, emotional distress, behavioral changes, and complex care needs. These experiences have taught me the importance of patience, active listening, sound judgment, and maintaining a calm, reassuring presence when someone is experiencing a crisis. I understand that behind every challenging behavior is an individual who deserves to be heard, respected, and treated with dignity.

My professional background has also strengthened my ability to recognize changes in behavior, communicate concerns effectively, maintain accurate documentation, and collaborate with multidisciplinary care teams. I recognize the importance of confidentiality, professional boundaries, and timely communication, particularly when the safety and well-being of vulnerable individuals are involved.

Although much of my direct care experience has been with older adults, I believe the fundamental skills of empathy, emotional awareness, adaptability, and crisis communication translate meaningfully into adolescent mental health services. I am especially interested in the opportunity to support teenagers during some of their most vulnerable moments, helping create an environment where they feel safe, understood, and supported without judgment.

I bring more than professional experience to this opportunity. I bring a genuine desire to make a positive difference, a willingness to continue learning, and an understanding that meaningful care begins with human connection. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute these qualities to a team dedicated to supporting adolescent mental health and connecting young people and their families with appropriate resources.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, interpersonal skills, and commitment to compassionate care align with your organization's mission.

Sincerely,
Sarah Granados

candidates.summary:
I have first hand experience being the first person someone talks to when working at Bellevue Clubhouse. I spent a lot of time at the front desk, scheduling people, answering the phone, and navigating virtual work when COVID hit. 
My experience with substance use comes from my time working on crisis lines when callers/texters would share they struggled with substances. I was able to be a listening ear and provide validation and meet them where they were at. Sometimes this meant they were open to receiving resources and I was able to work with them to find those.

work_history.title: Crisis Intervention Specialist
work_history.summary: Through Crisis Connections I answered chat and texts on 988 which is the suicide and crisis lifeline. I have honed in on my skills as a Crisis Specialist with focus on validation, empathy, and safety planning. I worked with staff such as clinicians to provide the best support for our help seekers. It was a busy job, sometimes taking two chats at a time, but it has helped me continue to work to help others and grow myself in terms of providing support efficiently.

work_history.title: Crisis Counselor
work_history.summary: At NYC Well, a crisis support line, I was a Crisis Counselor. We got calls from those with mental health problems and even sometimes calls forwarded from the National Suicide Prevention Line. This was a job I enjoyed because I was able to talk to those struggling, and bring them hope. Some calls lead to me finding resources to support them with their mental health, some to just talk to someone in need of a listening ear, and some lead to safety planning when a person was having active suicidal ideation. This job taught me how to deal with those suffering from a crisis, what safety planning is, and how important it is that clients have ongoing mental health care. I talked to many people of different genders, ages, sexual orientations, and religions and learned the importance of active listening, and providing validation.

work_history.title: Rehabilitation Associate
work_history.summary: I worked at Bellevue Clubhouse as a Rehabilitation Associate to then an Employment Specialist. Through Bellevue Clubhouse I have been able to learn the non-clinical model used to help adults with a mental health diagnoses. Through the Work Ordered Day (WOD), members can choose from an array of tasks to work on, such as data entry, personal advocacy, and much more. The member has the choice to choose to work on whatever interests them most. My job was to help engage members, work side by side with them, and assist in any way I could. Then as an Employment Specialist to help those interested in working again. From learning what they wanted from working, any worries they had, to helping them apply. From this job I learned I like working with people one on one to solve problems, or help improve their situations.

work_history.title: Front Desk Receptionist
work_history.summary: For about a year, while in school I decided to get a job. I wanted to see what it was like to work in a different environment than I have previously become acquainted with. For this reason I applied to the Sheraton in downtown Seattle and was given the opportunity to be a Front Desk Associate. This position helped me learn about the hospitality industry. On busy days I interacted with hundreds of customers. It was important to always be very professional and friendly in this environment. To me the best part of this job was the coworkers because they made coming in to work enjoyable. I feel like it is important for me to have a workplace where I like my coworkers because that really sets the tone of the job. I ended up stopping working there in July as I was almost done with school and ready to take a break from all things school are work related. I think the most rewarding part of the job was just any appreciation that verified I was doing my job well. I remember one person just thanking me for listening to what they had to say and reminded me that listening and helping others is really all I would like to do. Internship Seattle Children's Seattle, WA

work_history.title: Title Unknown
work_history.summary: This is an internship I was required to complete for my major at UW. I absolutely loved it. It was at the Psychiatry and Behavioral Medicine Unit at Seattle Children's Hospital. This unit is for children's who are in high crisis in respect to their mental health. The age range on the unit is from 3-18 and even older for those with developmental delays. I would go once a week for an eight hour work shift. I was able to choose which age group I wanted to work with and was able to work with all of them throughout my time there. This unit helps ensure safety of these children, provide stability and short term care, educate the patients and their families, and help hone in on coping skills. I loved getting to know the kids, and being able to discuss their mental health with them. The first few weeks were strictly for observation. As the time progressed I was able to start charting, and leading groups with patients and I felt comfortable in doing so. In the future I hope to work with a wider array of patients because this group was solely children. I also wasn't allowed to work with patients on the Autism Spectrum, low stimulation or those with eating disorders, as I would need more training before being able to do so. Completing this internship was difficult for me because of my connection to the children empathetic nature. Something we were supposed to do was leave work at work, and I had difficulty with that sometimes. It was however also very rewarding for me to work with the group of kids and get to know them. This internship was important for me because it verified that doing work along these lines is something I would like to do.

work_history.title: Gymnastics Coach
work_history.summary: While working at SGA, I have worked as a special events worker and as a coach. During special events, mostly birthday parties, I am one of the two staff members in charge, at the party. The job entitled me to act as a coach in the gym, and a helper in the party room. On the floor I would help children practice skills, and ensure they were being safe. In the party room I would help parents with things such as passing out food, and making sure things were going as planned. It is very important for us to keep the kids and parents happy, so I have learned a lot about customer service through this job. As a coach, I have been able to learn and work on leading groups of children, and teaching them new skills as well as practicing old ones. By being a coach I have improved my leadership skills, understanding the environment, and working under pressure. Sometimes kids don't listen, so you quickly have to assess and think of the right way to handle the situation appropriately. This was my first job and I had it in high school and I even returned recently to it to become a coach because of I love working with kids. To this day although I am not a regular coach, I sometimes am a substitute. Sales Associate Macy's Seattle, WA December 2015 to January 2016 I worked at Macy's for a few months in the Winter of 2015-2016 as a seasonal worker. I was a sales associate and I helped assist customers. This included being able to help them buy/return/exchange merchandise. We were trained to be polite, helpful, and knowledgeable. In order to make the customer's trip as convenient as possible it was important for us to be aware of availability of products among other things. Through Macy's I was able to gain retail skills, improve my customer service skills, as well as improve working at a register.

In my current role as a Case Manager at EMC Behavioral, I work in a fully virtual environment, supporting children and adolescents experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. My responsibilities include conducting intake assessments, identifying service needs, verifying insurance, coordinating referrals, scheduling appointments, and maintaining accurate client documentation. Working remotely has strengthened my ability to independently manage my responsibilities, communicate effectively with clients and caregivers through virtual platforms, and ensure timely follow-up without requiring daily in-person supervision. My work involves providing trauma-informed support, assisting with behavioral and emotional challenges, communicating with residents, and maintaining accurate documentation. Working with individuals during vulnerable periods has taught me the importance of approaching difficult conversations with empathy, patience, and professionalism while helping individuals feel respected and supported.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because both programs serve populations with whom I have direct professional experience. I believe that providing clear information, listening without judgment, and following through on next steps can make a meaningful difference in their willingness and ability to access care. My experience with insurance verification, intake coordination, appointment scheduling, and client communication, combined with my ability to work independently in a fully remote environment, aligns closely with the responsibilities of this position.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my behavioral health experience, organizational skills, and bilingual communication abilities to your admissions team. Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Remote Intake Coordinator position with your adolescent mental health facility. With previous experience as a Psychiatric Technician at an adolescent inpatient psychiatric hospital, as well as experience working as an Intake Coordinator at an alcohol and drug treatment facility, I bring a strong combination of hands-on behavioral health experience and patient intake coordination.

My experience working in adolescent inpatient psychiatry has given me a firsthand understanding of the challenges that adolescents and their families face when seeking mental health treatment. I understand the importance of compassion, patience, professionalism, and creating a supportive environment for individuals during what can often be an overwhelming and vulnerable time.

Additionally, my background in intake coordination within a substance use treatment setting has provided me with experience navigating the admissions process, communicating with individuals seeking treatment, gathering necessary information, and helping coordinate access to appropriate care. I understand how important it is to make the intake process as smooth, supportive, and efficient as possible.

I am especially interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to combine my experience in behavioral health with my passion for helping adolescents and families access the care they need. I would bring strong communication skills, empathy, attention to detail, and a genuine commitment to making a positive difference in the lives of those seeking support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience could contribute to your team. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely, 
Lauren Huttunen

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my enthusiastic interest in joining your team to support children, youth, and families. With a strong academic foundation in child development and human services, combined with extensive personal experience caring for and guiding young people, I bring a practical, empathetic, and dedicated skill set that aligns directly with the demands of child welfare and social work.

Throughout my educational coursework and hands-on experience with children and adolescents across various age groups, I have built a deep understanding of developmental milestones, behavioral dynamics, and trauma-informed support. My background has prepared me to handle the core responsibilities of child-centered advocacy, including:

Crisis De-escalation & Emotional Support: Applying patience, active listening, and calm guidance to help youth navigate emotional distress, behavioral challenges, and difficult life transitions.

Child Safety & Behavioral Observation: Maintaining a safe, structured, and protective environment while staying attentive to subtle changes in a child’s physical, emotional, or social well-being.

Care Coordination & Advocacy: Organizing daily routines, supporting educational and developmental goals, and advocating for the best interests of youth in both individual and group settings.

Cultural Sensitivity & Communication: Interacting respectfully with diverse families and youth, maintaining clear boundaries, and upholding strict standards of confidentiality and professional ethics.

My passion for this field comes from a fundamental belief that every child deserves a safe, supportive foundation to grow and succeed. While my background is built on targeted coursework and intensive personal caregiving rather than standard corporate roles, this path has provided me with real-world resilience, adaptability, and an authentic understanding of the day-to-day needs of youth.

I am eager to bring my work ethic, baseline knowledge, and strong commitment to child advocacy to your organization. Thank you for your time and consideration, and I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my experience fits your team's current needs.

Sincerely,

River B. Marlioni

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

When someone finally makes the decision to call for mental health or substance use treatment, how they are treated during that first conversation matters. They may be scared, overwhelmed, frustrated, or simply unsure of what to do next. That is why I am especially interested in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. My experience in behavioral health admissions and intake has taught me how to meet people where they are while still guiding a conversation toward a productive next step. I am comfortable speaking with prospective clients and families, collecting sensitive information, answering questions, coordinating the admissions process, completing documentation, and following up consistently. I also bring the self-direction needed for remote admissions work. I am comfortable managing my own workload and pipeline, keeping track of multiple conversations and next steps, and working within CRM and EMR systems to maintain accurate, confidential records. I believe strong admissions work comes down to both compassion and consistency. People deserve to feel cared for during the conversation, and they also deserve to know that someone will actually follow through afterward. The opportunity to support two programs serving different populations is especially meaningful to me. Whether the person reaching out is a parent trying to find help for their teenager or an adult considering treatment for substance use and mental health concerns, I would approach that conversation with patience, professionalism, and respect. I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my admissions experience, communication skills, reliability, and commitment to helping people access care to your team. Thank you for considering my application and I look forward to speaking with you.

Sincerely,
Savannah Szwarc

I am eager to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. As a Master of Social Work graduate with extensive experience supporting individuals grappling with mental health, substance use, academic, and life challenges, I possess the communication, assessment, and care coordination skills necessary to assist clients and families in taking the pivotal initial steps toward treatment.

Throughout my career, I have collaborated with individuals during challenging and uncertain periods, enabling them to navigate services, identify resources, and progress with confidence. As a Student Success Coach at Tallahassee State College, I managed a high-volume caseload while conducting outreach through phone, email, and text messaging, coordinating referrals, maintaining meticulous documentation, and providing support to students through enrollment and assistance processes. My responsibilities necessitated strong follow-through, attention to detail, and the ability to establish trust rapidly with individuals from diverse backgrounds.

In addition to my higher education experience, my social work training and internships provided direct experience working with individuals affected by substance use disorders, mental health concerns, trauma, and involvement in the criminal justice system. I conducted assessments, facilitated group therapy sessions, connected clients to services, and assisted individuals in overcoming barriers to care. These experiences enhanced my capacity to listen with empathy, remain composed in emotionally charged situations, and communicate clearly about available options and subsequent steps.

I am proficient in working independently in a remote environment, managing multiple priorities, maintaining accurate records, and handling sensitive information with professionalism and confidentiality. Most importantly, I recognize that the initial interaction an individual has with a treatment provider can significantly influence their willingness to seek assistance. I am committed to ensuring that every person feels heard, respected, and supported, even when the outcome may be a referral to another resource.

I would be honored to bring my behavioral health background, client-centered approach, and strong organizational skills to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I eagerly anticipate the opportunity to discuss how my experience can contribute to the vital work being undertaken at Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Aray Schuman
Macon, Missouri

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With several years of experience working in human services, crisis intervention, and youth and family support, I believe I bring a strong combination of compassion, communication skills, and organizational experience that would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role with Safe Passage Violence Prevention Center, I work closely with children, adolescents, and families who are navigating difficult and often traumatic circumstances. My responsibilities include crisis intervention, case management, safety planning, coordinating referrals, communicating with community partners, and maintaining confidential documentation. This work has taught me the importance of meeting people where they are, listening without judgment, and helping individuals and families navigate overwhelming situations with compassion and understanding.

One of the things I value most about my work is being able to help people during some of their most difficult moments. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming step for both adolescents and their families. I believe the first interaction can make a lasting impression, and I would take pride in helping families feel heard, supported, and comfortable as they navigate the admissions process.

In addition to my direct service experience, I bring strong administrative and communication skills, experience handling sensitive information, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple responsibilities. I am comfortable working with diverse populations, collaborating with professionals across different service areas, and adapting to situations that require patience, professionalism, and sound judgment.

I am interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to continue making a difference in the lives of adolescents and families while growing professionally in the behavioral health field. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, work ethic, and genuine passion for helping others to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Aray Schuman

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I’ve spent more than 20 years in education, mostly working with middle and high school students in special education. I also have three years of experience as a mental health professional, including two and a half years with Pelican Bay Agency. What drew me to this position is the chance to help teens and their families when they know they need support but aren’t sure where to start.

At Pelican Bay Agency, I worked with children, adults, and families when one or more family members were going through a crisis. I provided crisis intervention, listened to what was happening, and helped them work through the situation and figure out what to do next. That experience taught me how important it is to stay calm, listen first, and explain things in a way people can understand when they already have a lot on their minds.

I took that same approach in education. I remember helping a student who wanted to go to cosmetology school but was overwhelmed by the application and financial aid paperwork. We broke it down together, called the school, and connected with an advisor who helped her get enrolled. I enjoyed that part of my job because I could help someone take a step they weren’t sure how to take on their own.

That’s what I’d bring to your admissions team. When a parent calls about mental health or substance use treatment for their teen, I’d give them room to talk, explain what comes next, and follow up when I say I will. I know that first call can be hard to make, and I’d want families to feel comfortable asking questions.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d appreciate the chance to talk with you about how my experience could help your team and the families you serve.

Sincerely,
Anthony DeVoil

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With over 25 years of experience in healthcare and more than eight years dedicated to addiction recovery services, I bring a unique combination of clinical support experience, administrative coordination, leadership, and genuine compassion for individuals and families navigating difficult circumstances.

During my time as a Recovery Care Technician Supervisor and Medical Assistant at the Arbor, I worked closely with individuals experiencing substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health challenges. My responsibilities included coordinating admissions and discharges, collaborating with clinical teams, overseeing medication reconciliation and documentation, and supporting clients throughout their treatment experience. Supervising a team of approximately 15 staff members while helping coordinate care for roughly 40 clients strengthened my ability to remain organized, communicate effectively, and approach sensitive situations with patience and professionalism.

In my current role with Anthony Medical & Chiropractic, I have further developed my expertise in insurance verification, benefits coordination, patient scheduling, authorization requirements, and electronic medical records. These responsibilities align closely with your need for an admissions professional who can efficiently guide individuals from their initial inquiry through assessment scheduling and intake.

What particularly draws me to this opportunity is your commitment to being the first compassionate voice someone hears when seeking help. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment often requires tremendous courage, especially for adolescents and their families. I believe that listening without judgment, providing clear information, and following through with consistency can make a meaningful difference in someone's willingness to begin treatment.

My professional philosophy is rooted in compassionate communication, accountability, and meeting people where they are. I am comfortable managing multiple responsibilities independently, maintaining accurate and confidential documentation, and working collaboratively to ensure individuals receive appropriate care.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and understanding of the recovery process to your admissions team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to discussing how my background and approach to patient care align with your organization's mission.

Sincerely,

Jody Sonnier

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my strong interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a trained Registered Behavioral Technician (RBT) with hands-on experience supporting youth through structured interventions, skill-building, and crisis de-escalation, I am deeply drawn to your mission of providing compassionate, comprehensive mental health and wellness care for teens.
In my work as an RBT, I have developed a calm, observant, and client-centered approach to behavioral support. My daily responsibilities have centered on implementing individualized treatment plans, facilitating positive peer interactions, and supporting emotional regulation during group transitions and challenging moments. Key strengths I bring to Adolescent Wellness Academy include:
• Behavioral & Emotional Support: Utilizing positive reinforcement, redirection, and structured routines to help young clients navigate frustration, build coping skills, and stay engaged in therapeutic activities.
• Collaborative Care: Partnering closely with Board Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBAs) and multidisciplinary teams to probe new skills, adjust protocols, and maintain safe, supportive environments.
• Objective Documentation: Maintaining accurate, detailed, and insurance-compliant session records that clearly track client progress, demeanor, and behavioral patterns.
I admire Adolescent Wellness Academy’s commitment to helping adolescents heal, connect, and grow together. My background in behavioral health equips me to step seamlessly into a fast-paced clinical or residential setting, build genuine rapport with teens, and uphold the highest standards of patient safety and care.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my RBT training and passion for youth development can support your clinical team and the adolescents you serve.
Sincerely,
Sarah Hall

Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. For more than two years, I have been the person families reach on the hardest day of their lives. I handle the full admissions process, from first contact to completed admission. I am comfortable working remotely and independently. I serve as a remote on-call clinician twice weekly from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m., handling admissions without direct supervision. Before that, I worked full-time as a remote medical scribe for University of Wisconsin Medical. I have extensive EMR experience with Meditech, Epic, MyChart, and SmartCare, and I learn new systems quickly. I speak intermediate Spanish.

Frightened callers need calm, plain language. My training in de-escalation and tactical communication helps me provide it. So does my background teaching about 500 college students, which taught me to explain complex information patiently. I would welcome the chance to bring this experience to your adolescent and adult programs.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how I can support your admissions team.

Sincerely, 

Michael P. Berte

I have extensive EMR experience with Meditech, Epic, MyChart, and SmartCare, and I learn new systems quickly. I speak intermediate Spanish. I hold HIPAA, CPR/AED, and Handle with Care ceritification. Cover Letter
Amanda Marshel
618-472-4725
amandamarshel320@gmail.com
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with your adolescent mental health and substance use treatment program.
Throughout my professional experience, I have developed strong communication, organization, leadership, and interpersonal skills. My background includes working as a paraprofessional at Wayne City Grade School, working with Child and Family Connections, and owning and operating Alphabet Kids Childcare Center for four years. These experiences have taught me the importance of patience, compassion, dependability, and building trusting relationships with children and families.
Mental health is something I understand on a personal level. Having faced my own mental health challenges, I recognize how difficult it can be to ask for help and how important it is to have someone who listens, understands, and offers support without judgment. These experiences have given me a genuine passion for helping others, especially adolescents who may be struggling and families searching for answers and support.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. The opportunity to be the person who helps someone take that first step toward receiving support is especially meaningful to me. I believe that when people reach out during a difficult time, being met with patience, compassion, and a calm and reassuring voice can make a real difference.

In my recent role as an Eligibility Specialist with the Department of Family Resources, I worked directly with clients to assist with applications, case maintenance, and interviews related to SNAP, TANF, and Health Coverage. This experience taught me how important it is to listen carefully, communicate clearly, protect sensitive information, and help people navigate processes that can feel confusing or overwhelming.

My previous work in education has also shaped the way I approach supporting others. As a Paraprofessional and Instructional Assistant, I worked closely with students with special needs, including providing one-on-one support and implementing behavior-management strategies. I learned to be patient, observant, adaptable, and compassionate while building trusting relationships with students, families, and staff. I understand that every individual has different needs and that sometimes the most important thing you can do is simply listen and meet someone where they are.

I also bring several years of experience as a small-business owner, where I independently managed client relationships, scheduling, records, customer communication, and day-to-day operations. That experience taught me the importance of follow-through, organization, professionalism, and taking ownership of my responsibilities without needing constant direction.

Although my background has not been specifically in behavioral-health or substance-use admissions, the common thread throughout my career has been helping people, communicating with them respectfully, and making sure their needs are heard and addressed. I am eager to bring those skills to an admissions environment and learn the specific processes and systems needed to help your clients and families successfully move toward care.

I would be honored to have the opportunity to contribute to a team whose work can make such an important difference in the lives of adolescents, adults, and their families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about how my experience, compassion, and dedication to helping others could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,

Miranda Baker

Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Reaching out for mental health or substance use support is often one of the hardest steps a person or family can take, and I want to be the steady, supportive first voice who helps them figure out their next steps. With a Master of Social Work, hands-on behavioral health intake experience, and a background managing multi-site outreach and call center operations, I am well-suited for a fully remote admissions role.

Throughout my behavioral health career, including my roles as a Program Supervisor and Social Worker at WellLife Network's Community Residence and as an Adult Care Manager at the Association for Mental Health and Wellness, I worked directly with individuals and families facing acute mental health challenges. At WellLife Network, I completed intake assessments and CANS (Child and Adolescent Needs and Strengths) assessments, partnered with clients and families on treatment planning and regular goal reviews, and helped coordinate transitions into the right level of care. That work taught me how to ask sensitive questions with patience, explain treatment options clearly without unnecessary clinical language, and keep accurate, HIPAA-compliant records in electronic health systems.

I am also comfortable working independently in fast-paced environments that require strong organization and consistent follow-through. While working as a Call Center Assistant Manager and In-House Marketing Agent with Wyndham Destinations and Capital Vacations, I managed inbound and outbound call pipelines, coordinated scheduling across 10 to 15 East Coast sites, and logged every inquiry in our CRM so no one fell through the cracks. Combined with my experience in Microsoft Word, Excel, and daily reporting, I know how to manage my own schedule, meet deadlines without close supervision, and stay on top of every lead until they are scheduled or connected with appropriate care.

I would appreciate the chance to bring my clinical background, intake experience, and self-directed work style to your company. Thank you for your time and consideration, and I look forward to speaking with you.

Sincerely,

Natashia Szumczyk

candidates.cover_letter:
November 19, 2026
Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy & Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Team,

Your posting says many callers reach out on one of the hardest days of their lives. For four and a half years, I was the person on the other end of that moment. I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role, where I can keep helping people take that first step into care.

At Aware Recovery Care, a yearlong in-home addiction treatment program, I worked fully remote as a Family Education Facilitator. My title wasn’t admissions, but at its core my role was the same: I was the first voice families heard, and my job was to help them say yes to care. Before each first call, I reviewed the client’s background so I could meet the family where they were. Many were scared, skeptical, or exhausted. I built trust, explained the treatment process in plain and caring language, and followed up consistently
until they were enrolled and taking part. When our program wasn’t the right fit, I connected them with resources and a clear next step.

I am also comfortable working on my own. After a 2024 restructuring, I was chosen to help build out Aware’s family department and eventually became its only member, supporting families across all 11 states. I managed my own caseload, outreach, and follow-up without daily direction, and I documented every contact in our EHR accurately and in line with HIPAA. I learn new systems quickly and would be glad to get up to speed on Kipu and your CRM.

My master’s in psychology from Harvard focused on why family involvement matters in addiction treatment. That is why AWA’s work with teens and their families, and PRC’s care for adults with co-occurring conditions, both mean a lot to me. I would bring real compassion and steady follow-through to every caller.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can support
your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Pamela Ardizzone

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a bachelor's degree in Psychology and Sociology and experience working in behavioral health, crisis intervention, and adolescent assessment, I have found that supporting individuals and families through difficult situations is work I genuinely care about. I would love the opportunity to bring that experience to your team.

In my current role as a Case Manager with Clarvida, I work with both adults and youth experiencing behavioral health crises. A big part of my role involves listening to clients and their families, understanding their needs, worries, and concerns, coordinating services, and helping them navigate, what can often be, an overwhelming time in their lives. Before this, I worked as an Assessment Center Specialist with AmeriCorps at The Village in Pocatello, Idaho, where I conducted youth and family assessments, completed structured screenings, and helped connect families with the resources and support they needed.

What interests me most about this position is the opportunity to be one of the first people families interact with when seeking help for their child. I understand that reaching out for mental health support can be a difficult and sometimes intimidating experience, and I think having someone who is patient, approachable, and genuinely willing to listen can make a meaningful difference. I would love to be that person for families beginning their journey with Adolescent Wellness Academy.

I also bring experience working with virtual platforms through my previous role as a Zoom Video Monitor at Idaho State University, where I managed online classroom operations and troubleshot technical issues. Combined with my background in documentation, communication, and coordinating care, I feel confident in my ability to adapt to a virtual admissions environment.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would be excited to bring my experience, compassion, and enthusiasm for helping others to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I appreciate the opportunity to be considered and hope to speak with you soon!

Sincerely,
Taylor Consigny

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor’s degree in Human Services and hands-on experience as a Visitation Coordinator with Job and Family Services, I am excited about the opportunity to support teens and families as the compassionate first point of contact on their path to care.
In my role as Visitation Coordinator for Job and Family Services, I regularly worked with families navigating high-stress, emotionally charged situations. I coordinated schedules, communicated clearly with parents, caseworkers, maintained accurate documentation, and ensured that processes ran smoothly while prioritizing the well-being of the children and families involved. This experience strengthened my ability to listen with empathy, explain procedures in plain language, manage multiple moving parts, and follow through consistently—skills that transfer directly to guiding families through the admissions process.
My Bachelor’s degree in Human Services provided a strong foundation in family systems, crisis intervention, ethical practice, and the social factors that influence adolescent mental health. I am well prepared to conduct sensitive screenings, explain levels of care in a clear and caring way, coordinate intake documentation and insurance verification, and track leads accurately in CRM/EMR systems while maintaining HIPAA compliance. I am comfortable working independently in a remote environment and managing my own pipeline with strong organization and follow-through.
I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s specialized focus on adolescents ages 13–17 and its commitment to evidence-based, family-centered care. I understand that many families reach out on some of the hardest days of their lives, and I am committed to meeting those callers with patience, respect, and hope. I would be proud to help teens and their families take that important first step toward feeling safe, connected, and supported.
Thank you for considering my application. Sincerely,

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With two and a half years of experience working within substance use disorder (SUD) and mental health treatment, I have developed a strong foundation in behavioral health, patient engagement, the intake processes, and case management. I believe my professional experience, interpersonal strengths, and commitment to helping individuals navigate the recovery process make me a strong candidate for this opportunity.

My experience in the behavioral health field includes working at both Twelve Oaks Recovery Center and Banyan Treatment Center, where I have spent approximately equal amounts of time developing my skills in treatment settings. At Twelve Oaks, I served as a Behavioral Health Technician and gained additional leadership experience as a Lead Technician. At Banyan, I continued working as a Behavioral Health Technician before transitioning into my current role as a Case Management and Clinical Intern at the BSW level. In this capacity, I have personally completed multiple case management intake assessments following patient admission and have written dozens of individual weekly progress notes for patients in the outpatient program. During my time as a BHT and throughout my internship I have had the opportunity to work in almost every section of Kipu, developing my understanding and ability to navigate the program effectively. These experiences have strengthened my understanding of patient needs, clinical documentation, communication, and the importance of establishing trust early in the treatment process.

Prior to entering the social work field, I worked as a Front Desk Attendant and Night Auditor with Marriott. Although this experience was outside of healthcare, it provided me with valuable opportunities to develop my problem-solving abilities, communication skills, and experience gathering and managing information during guest reception and registration. I have found that many of these skills translate directly into behavioral health admissions, where professionalism, patience, attention to detail, and the ability to connect with people are essential.

I consider my greatest strengths to be problem-solving, communication, determination, and compassion. Perhaps most importantly, I genuinely believe that all people are inherently good and deserve to be treated with dignity, understanding, and respect. This belief has shaped my approach to social work and my interactions with individuals navigating substance use and mental health challenges. I recognize that the admissions process can be an overwhelming and vulnerable experience for both adolescents and their families, and I would approach each interaction with empathy, patience, and a commitment to helping them feel heard and supported.

I am currently completing my Bachelor of Social Work degree, with an anticipated completion date of December 12, 2026. I have also completed CPR and SBIRT certifications, as well as CPI training, which has since expired. I am eager to continue expanding my knowledge and professional capabilities while building upon the experience I have gained in the behavioral health field.

I am particularly interested in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy because I see this position as an opportunity to broaden my experience in social work while continuing to serve individuals and families affected by mental health and substance use challenges. My background in treatment settings, familiarity with intake and case management processes including Kipu, and genuine passion for helping others would allow me to bring both practical experience and a compassionate perspective to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, strengths, and commitment to the behavioral health field could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,

William Chappell

I have a  diverse background in behavioral healthcare, facility management, student support, and customer service, therefore, I will continue to provide compassionate care, create welcoming environments, and ensure the safety and well-being of others. I am very dependable, approachable, organized, and attentive to the needs of every individual I assist. I believe my combination of hands-on care experience, leadership skills, and commitment to helping others would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role as a Mental Health Technician at Lincoln Trail Behavioral Health System, I work directly with patients to ensure safety, support, and comfortability. My responsibilities include conducting regular safety checks, assisting with daily living activities, documenting patient information, monitoring vital signs, and facilitating therapeutic group sessions focused on healthy behaviors and positive coping strategies. I also communicate with nursing staff regarding patient needs. If needed, I use crisis intervention and de-escalation techniques to help maintain a safe and supportive unit. This position has strengthened my patience, empathy, attention to detail, and ability to remain calm in challenging situations. Most importantly, it has taught me the importance of treating every individual with repsect and care.

My experience at UC Davis Student Unions has also equipped me with valuable customer service, administrative, and leadership skills. I’m applying for a position with Adolescent Wellness Academy because I want to continue working with teens in a setting where they feel understood and supported. I earned my B.S. in Psychology from Brigham Young University and bring experience as a registered behavior technician, as an intern at a youth crisis center, and as a psychology researcher.

During my internship at Wasatch Behavioral Health, I worked with therapists to develop a goal-setting activity for adolescents at the youth crisis center. We designed it to help teens connect a health goal to something they personally cared about and identify a step they felt ready to take. I enjoyed finding a way to make goal-setting feel relevant to each teen’s life. As a registered behavior technician, I also learned to provide consistent one-on-one support, adjust my communication to each client, and document progress while following individualized plans under supervision.

My research at BYU has given me another way to think about supporting behavior change. In the Health and Development Psychology Lab, I developed a proposal on how personal values might help people follow through on health goals. In the Personality and Close Relationships Lab, I analyzed open-ended responses for a first-author manuscript, which taught me to pay close attention to how people describe their experiences in their own words. As a lab manager, I coordinated meetings, delegated tasks, and kept track of project deadlines. I would bring that same attention to detail and follow-through to your team.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to helping teens feel safe and understood while working alongside families. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to that work through direct support, careful documentation, and collaboration with your clinical team. Thank you for considering my application.

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am pleased to introduce myself as an experienced, results-driven professional with an extensive 
background in business operations, account management, leadership, sales development, customer 
relations, and professional services. Throughout my career, I have continually expanded my expertise 
across a diverse range of industries, responsibilities, and professional environments. This breadth of 
experience has equipped me with an adaptable skill set, a strong business perspective, and the ability to
contribute meaningfully in a variety of organizational roles.
My professional background includes more than a decade of management and leadership experience, 
overseeing teams, developing employees, managing complex workflows, cultivating business 
relationships, and implementing strategies that improve performance and operational efficiency. I have 
developed and implemented comprehensive training programs, coached and mentored sales 
professionals, managed substantial customer and business account portfolios, and contributed to award
winning team performance. I take particular pride in helping individuals recognize their potential, 
develop their abilities, and achieve greater levels of professional success.
Beyond traditional management and account services, my experience encompasses business-to
business and business-to-consumer sales, financial services, client relations, operational management, 
project coordination, recruiting, onboarding, marketing, logistics, and process improvement. My 
entrepreneurial and freelance experience has further broadened my professional capabilities through 
business consultation, virtual assistance, proofreading, editing, administrative support, and social media
management. Working with clients across numerous professional sectors has strengthened my ability to
adapt quickly, understand different business needs, and navigate unfamiliar systems and 
responsibilities.
I also place considerable importance on continuous education and professional development. In 
addition to earning a Bachelor of Arts degree, I have completed approximately 1,000 advanced 
professional learning programs and certificates spanning management, leadership, business, finance, 
accounting, human resources, customer service, marketing, sales, communication, writing, technology, 
and personal development. I believe that remaining knowledgeable, adaptable, and willing to learn is 
essential to long-term professional success.
What I offer is more than experience in any single discipline. I bring a combination of leadership, 
analytical thinking, interpersonal communication, organizational ability, business awareness, and 
practical problem-solving skills. I am comfortable working independently or collaboratively, managing 
competing priorities, learning new systems, and taking ownership of responsibilities. Whether 
contributing to daily operations, developing business relationships, supporting organizational 
objectives, improving processes, or helping a team reach its potential, I approach my work with 
professionalism, dedication, and a commitment to meaningful results.
I welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, versatility, and work ethic to an organization that 
values initiative, professional development, and the contributions of capable individuals. I would 
appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background and abilities could complement your 
organization's needs and objectives.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.
Sincerely,
Scott Remaly
