candidates.cover_letter:
To whom it may concern,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. I am drawn to this opportunity because it combines compassionate communication, organization, and the ability to make a meaningful difference in the lives of adolescents.

I understand that reaching out for treatment can be an emotional and overwhelming experience. I believe every person deserves to feel heard and respected, as well as fully supported. I would bring a warm, professional, and patient approach to each interaction while helping prospective clients and their families understand their treatment options and also navigate the admissions process with confidence.

I am confident in my ability to manage multiple inquiries, maintain consistent follow-up, coordinate assessments and intake processes, and keep accurate records. I also understand the importance of confidentiality, attention to detail, and maintaining HIPAA-compliant documentation. Working remotely requires accountability, strong time management, and the ability to independently manage priorities, all of which I recognize as essential to succeeding in this position.

What particularly interests me about joining your team is the opportunity to be part of someone's first step toward healing. I would approach every interaction with compassion, professionalism, and a genuine commitment to helping people access the care they need. I have done my practicum for substance abuse counseling in an adolescent facility before and helping adolescents is something I have always strived to do. Whether helping as a teacher, guiding them to start a recovery process, or as an EKG technician as I am studying for. 

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my skills, dedication, and passion for helping others could contribute to your admissions team. I look forward to the possibility of joining your growing organization.

Sincerely,
Sarah Garcia

Adolescent Wellness Academy,

Hello, my name is Jada Schallhorn and I am excited to write to you about my interest in the Virtual Admission Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a passion for caring for teenagers with mental health disorders and substance abuse problems, and the ability to work in a fast-paced, customer-oriented environment, I am confident that my skills and personality will make me a great fit for this role.

As a social and detail oriented, I provide attentive care while executing plans and following through with their behavior plans while I worked as a Psychiatric Technician/Behavioral Health Professional. I do have experience of working with pre-teenagers and teenagers aged 10-18 that have a variety of mental disorders (PTSD, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, Bipolar disorder, Dissociative Identity Disorder, & more) and substance abuse problems. While I worked at Pine Rest Christian Mental Health services, I had experience of working with these individuals. We did teach these teenagers why substances are not good, and the detrimental impact it has on them in the long run. I also learned restorative approaches, had trauma informed care, and de-escalation techniques while working at this job. These techniques and approaches I learned help teach the client how to manage their emotions and triggers, ask for help in a healthy manner, and how to use coping skills during a crisis. The skills I used in that job will be useful while I work as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator. 

I have experience of working with elderly clients as a caregiver who have neurological conditions such as dementia, Alzheimer's, and clients whom also have mental disorders such as PTSD. I do use verbal de-escalation with these clients if they are escalated, I came up with ideas for solutions if there are conflicts, and I ensure my client is safe and comfortable with every interaction.

I do have experience of working with adults who have substance abuse problems. In 2019, I interned for a substance abuse counselor. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to be considered for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. My background in healthcare includes patient support, case management, insurance verification, authorizations, and healthcare coordination. Throughout my career, I have enjoyed helping people navigate what can often be a complicated healthcare system, and I believe my experience would translate well to this role.

In my previous positions with EVERSANA, I worked closely with patients and healthcare providers to navigate benefit investigations, coverage issues, authorizations, appeals, and patient assistance programs. I also gained leadership experience supervising a team responsible for patient access services, managing escalated cases, and ensuring patients received the support they needed. My current role with Conifer Health Solutions has further strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, maintain accuracy, and work independently in a remote healthcare environment.

I also bring a personal perspective that I believe would be valuable in this position. As a parent who has navigated the mental health system while advocating for my own child, I understand that seeking help for a child is not always an easy or straightforward process. There can be difficult decisions, uncertainty, fear, and a lot of questions along the way. I understand how important it is for parents to feel that someone is listening, taking their concerns seriously, and helping them understand the options available to their family. I know that the admissions process may be one of the first interactions a family has when reaching out for help, and I would approach those conversations with patience, compassion, and respect.

I would love the opportunity to bring my professional healthcare experience and personal understanding to your team. I believe I offer a combination of administrative knowledge, problem-solving skills, and genuine empathy that would allow me to make a positive contribution to both the admissions team and the families they serve.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and perspective could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,

Wendy Dalton

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Dear Hiring Team,
When a parent reaches out about their teen's mental health or substance use, that first call matters. They are often scared, tired and unsure where to start. I want to be the calm and caring voice that helps them take the next step. That is why I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role at Adolescent Wellness Academy.
I currently work as a Qualified Mental Health Professional (QMHP) with Exceptional Wellness Inc, where all of my work is done through telehealth. I reach out to parents, schedule first sessions and support clients through skills training, case management and crisis intervention. I am also certified in the CANS and ANSA assessments, so I am used to asking careful questions, gathering the right information and understanding what a family truly needs. Working remotely has taught me to manage my own caseload, stay organized and keep clear documentation on time.
Before this role, I worked for almost two years as a Registered Behavior Technician with children at BlueSprig Pediatrics and Twinkle Autism Therapy. Talking with parents was a big part of that work. I learned how to listen first, stay steady when emotions run high and explain next steps in a way families can follow. I also learned how much follow through matters. When I tell a family I will call them back, I do.
I hold a Bachelor's degree in Psychology from the University of Houston Clear Lake, and I am currently earning my Master's in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Our Lady of the Lake University. My graduate training helps me understand the concerns that bring families to treatment and the importance of getting teens the right level of care. I also grew up crossing the border between Mexico and the United States every day for school, and I speak English and Spanish fluently. This helps me connect with families from many different backgrounds.
I learn new systems quickly, and I would bring the same organization I use with my clients to tracking inquiries, following up with families and supporting enrollments in your CRM. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can help families at Adolescent Wellness Academy from their very first call. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Aranza Hernandez

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a professional background in legal intake, client relations, and high-volume customer service, I have developed a strong ability to communicate with individuals during sensitive and often overwhelming circumstances. I believe my experience, interpersonal skills, and genuine approach to helping others would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your admissions team.

In my current role as an Intake Specialist and Legal Assistant with the Law Offices of A. Sam Jubran, I serve as an initial point of contact for individuals seeking legal assistance. My responsibilities include conducting intake interviews, gathering sensitive personal information, assessing initial client needs, maintaining confidential records, and facilitating communication between clients, attorneys, and legal staff. This experience has taught me the importance of approaching every interaction with patience, empathy, professionalism, and an understanding that individuals may be reaching out during some of the most difficult moments in their lives.

I have learned that effective communication extends beyond simply answering questions or collecting information. It requires active listening, recognizing individual concerns, establishing trust, and helping people feel comfortable enough to share their circumstances without feeling judged or dismissed. I understand the importance of remaining compassionate while maintaining professional boundaries, protecting confidential information, and ensuring that individuals are connected with the appropriate resources and professionals.

Additionally, my previous experience as a Customer Service Expert with Select Portfolio Servicing strengthened my ability to manage a high volume of inbound and outbound calls, navigate sensitive financial matters, resolve concerns, and maintain effective communication in a remote work environment. These experiences have prepared me to manage the demands of a virtual admissions setting while remaining organized, attentive, and responsive.

What particularly interests me about Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to contribute to an organization focused on supporting adolescents and families who may be navigating challenging and life-changing circumstances. I recognize that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable decision for both adolescents and their families. I would approach those conversations with compassion, discretion, patience, and an understanding of the importance of making individuals feel supported throughout the admissions process.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my communication skills, administrative experience, and client-centered approach to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and professional strengths may align with the needs of your team.

Sincerely,
Charisma Brown

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. After reviewing the position, I was immediately drawn to the opportunity because it brings together two areas I am deeply passionate about: mental health care and helping individuals and families navigate some of the most difficult moments in their lives.

I bring eight years of experience working at Children’s Health Dallas, where I have had the opportunity to care for pediatric patients across various clinical settings, including the Emergency Department, intensive care, and inpatient units. A significant part of my experience has involved working directly with children and adolescents experiencing behavioral health emergencies, suicidal ideation, self-harm, and emotional crises. These experiences have taught me that the way we communicate with patients and families during vulnerable moments can make a lasting difference in their willingness to seek and accept help.

I earned my Bachelor of Science in Child Development and Family Studies with a concentration in Child Life and a minor in Psychology. I am now pursuing my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Walden University as a full-time graduate student, with an emphasis in Trauma and Crisis Counseling. Continuing my education in this field has only strengthened my commitment to supporting individuals experiencing mental health challenges, particularly children, adolescents, and their families.

Throughout my healthcare career, I have developed strong communication, organizational, and patient coordination skills. I understand the importance of listening without judgment, recognizing when someone may be in crisis, maintaining confidentiality, and communicating clearly with families and healthcare professionals. My experience in both direct patient care and healthcare education has also prepared me to manage competing responsibilities, maintain detailed documentation, and approach sensitive conversations with patience and professionalism.

What stands out to me most about this opportunity is the responsibility of being the first person someone speaks with when reaching out for help. I understand that making that initial call can be incredibly difficult, especially for a parent concerned about their child’s mental health or an individual seeking substance use treatment. I would take that responsibility seriously and strive to ensure every caller feels heard, respected, and supported while being guided toward the appropriate next steps.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my clinical background, knowledge of adolescent behavioral health, and genuine passion for mental health advocacy to your admissions team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and dedication align with the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

candidates.summary:
I am a dedicated healthcare professional with extensive experience in pediatric patient care, behavioral health, and clinical support, including eight years of experience at Children’s Health Dallas. Throughout my career, I have worked closely with children and adolescents experiencing mental health crises, suicidal ideation, self-harm, emotional distress, and complex medical conditions. My experience includes supporting patients and families in emergency and inpatient settings, assisting with patient safety and crisis de-escalation, collaborating with multidisciplinary healthcare teams, and maintaining accurate, confidential medical documentation.

I hold a Bachelor of Science in Child Development and Family Studies with a concentration in Child Life and a minor in Psychology. I am currently a full-time graduate student at Walden University pursuing my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with an emphasis in Trauma and Crisis Counseling. My education, combined with my clinical experience, has strengthened my understanding of adolescent mental health, trauma-informed care, family dynamics, and the importance of compassionate communication during vulnerable moments.

In addition to my pediatric and behavioral health background, I have experience in healthcare administration, patient communication, clinical coordination, and medical education. I am comfortable communicating with patients, families, and healthcare professionals, navigating sensitive situations, and helping individuals understand the next steps in their care.

I am particularly interested in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position because it combines my experience in behavioral health and patient-centered communication with my long-term commitment to improving access to mental health services. I understand how overwhelming seeking treatment can be for individuals and families, and I would bring compassion, professionalism, strong organizational skills, and a genuine dedication to helping people access the care they need.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy, 

I am writing to express my interest in joining the Adolescent Wellness Academy team. Having worked in inpatient mental health treatment, substance use treatment, and healthcare customer service, I have a deep understanding of the value of patient-centered, compassionate care. I am especially drawn to AWA's goal of establishing a secure setting where adolescents struggling with mental health and substance use issues feel valued, understood, and supported.

My interest in behaviroal health is both professional and deeply personal. I experienced the loss of my late partner to suicide. He was an Army veteran who struggled with PTSD, mental health challenges, and substance use following his deployment. Witnessing the difficulties he faced in navigating life after military service at such a young age profoundly influenced my understanding of the connection between mental health, addiction, and access to meaningful support. His story is a significant part of why I chose this career path. I hope to contribute to a future where individuals and families feel less alone when navigating these challenges. 

Professionally, I have gained hands-on experience supporting adolescents and adults in inpatient psychiatric settings at Snowden at Fredericksburg, as well as individuals receiving substance use treatment at Warsaw Recovery Center. My responsibilities have allowed me to develop skills in patient observation, therapeutic communication, documentation, and maintaining safe and supportive treatment environments. I also bring experience with electronic health record systems, including Epic and Kipu, along with a background in healthcare technology and customer support through TELUS Health.

My long-term goal is to obtain my clinical licensure and specialize in mental health and addiction therapy. I recognize that this journey requires continued education, professional development, supervision, and a willingness to learn. I am not entering this field with the expectation that I can save anyone. When a parent calls about a teenager in crisis, or an adult finally reaches out about their drinking or drug use, that first conversation often decides whether they take the next step. I have spent 20 years in human services helping people through exactly those moments, and I would like to bring that experience to your Virtual Admissions Coordinator role supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

That background lines up with both of your programs: adolescent mental health care and adult substance use treatment with co-occurring conditions.
Good admissions work depends on follow-through, and that is where I am strongest. I don't let a person fall through the cracks between the first call and an intake date. I hold a Master of Social Work from Florida State University and a BA in Psychology from Gustavus Adolphus College. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can help your callers move from that first call to a clear next step. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With my hands-on experience working in adolescent residential behavioral health, I have developed a strong understanding of the challenges youth and their families face when navigating mental health treatment. I am passionate about helping individuals access the care they need and would love the opportunity to contribute to your admissions team.

I currently work as a Residential Behavioral Health Worker at Mary Hill Youth & Family Center through Integrated Services for Behavioral Health, where I provide direct support to adolescent girls ages 13–17. In this role, I work closely with youth experiencing a variety of mental health and behavioral challenges. My responsibilities include assisting with crisis de-escalation, providing emotional support, maintaining a safe and structured environment, documenting client behaviors and progress, and communicating with other staff members to ensure consistent care.

One of the most valuable things I have learned from working in residential treatment is how important compassion, patience, and communication are when supporting individuals during difficult moments. I have worked with adolescents who struggle to express their emotions, manage challenging situations, and adjust to receiving treatment. These experiences have taught me how to listen without judgment, build trust, and help individuals feel heard and supported.

I am especially interested in this position because I understand how difficult the decision to seek mental health treatment can be for both adolescents and their families. Having worked directly with youth in a treatment setting, I recognize the importance of making that first interaction a positive and reassuring experience. I would be excited to help families understand their options, answer questions, coordinate next steps, and make the admissions process feel less overwhelming.

In addition to my residential behavioral health experience, my education at Ohio University has strengthened my knowledge of healthcare and patient-centered communication. I am organized, dependable, comfortable handling sensitive information, and able to remain professional in fast-paced and emotionally challenging situations.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my residential treatment experience, compassion, and dedication to behavioral health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience could benefit your team.

Sincerely,
Makalin Stadtler

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to have the opportunity to apply to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Your mission to create a safe, compassionate, and supportive environment for adolescents facing mental health challenges aligns closely with my values, education, and experience. I am passionate about helping others feel seen, heard, and valued, and I welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team making a meaningful difference in young people's lives.

I hold a bachelor's degree in Psychology with a minor in Family Science and am currently pursuing a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling. I have four years of experience as a Registered Behavior Technician, providing one-on-one support to children and adolescents up to age 18 on the autism spectrum in home and clinical settings. In this role, I implemented evidence-based interventions, monitored client progress through data collection, and maintained a safe, supportive environment. As an Intervention Specialist, I also supported elementary-aged students with their academic, behavioral, and individual needs.

Beyond my direct experience working with children, I have developed strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills. In my role leading volunteer operations for my church, I had the privilege of training and supervising more than 30 volunteers a day, ranging in age from 18 to 98. Working with such a diverse group taught me the importance of humility, adaptability, active listening, and recognizing different learning styles. I worked to create an inclusive environment where every individual felt heard and valued while helping improve daily operations through collaboration and individualized training. I also provided administrative support by answering phones, assisting visitors, responding to questions, and coordinating schedules.

I am drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy because of your commitment to connection, compassion, and individualized care. I believe one of the most meaningful things we can offer is a place where individuals feel safe to be themselves and know they are not alone and that they have value and purpose. 

Thank you for considering my application. I would be grateful for the chance to join your team and support the important work you do.

Sincerely, Kaley Rhoton

Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center,

I am very excited for the opportunity to work with your team as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator. I am a hard worker, a quick learner, and an empathetic leader who takes action. When families and individuals reach out on some of the hardest days of their lives, it is my goal to make sure that every person I speak with receives the care, guidance, and clear information they need to take that next step toward healing.

Having spent years working in crisis listening, wellness support, and youth and family education, I know how to hold a calm, non-judgmental space for someone in distress while still keeping things moving forward. Through my work with Kindly Human and my own holistic practice, I answer real-time audio and text inquiries from people navigating acute stress and emotional overwhelm, helping them feel heard while guiding them toward practical next steps. In my work running Lion English Academy and leading wellness programs, I have also worked closely with teenagers and parents going through difficult life transitions, explaining program options in plain, caring language and building real trust with families.

Emily Rivera

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With experience in healthcare-related customer service, insurance verification, administrative support, and handling sensitive information, I believe I could bring valuable skills to your team.

In my current position with Signature Performance, I work directly with medical professionals and members to assist with medical claims and verification of benefits. My previous experience in administrative support and help desk operations has also helped me develop strong organizational, problem-solving, and follow-through skills. I would welcome the opportunity to use my healthcare and customer service experience to help individuals and families navigate that process.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Saleh Delana

candidates.cover_letter:
Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over 30 years of experience in Medical Office Administration, I bring an extensive background in healthcare operations, patient coordination, and admissions, including experience in mental health, acute care, and emergency department settings.

Throughout my career, I have developed strong administrative and communication skills, with a particular focus on managing admissions processes, coordinating patient needs, and providing compassionate and professional service. I understand the importance of making individuals and families feel welcomed, supported, and informed, especially when navigating the challenges associated with mental health and substance abuse treatment.

I offer excellent telephone etiquette, strong organizational skills, and the ability to prioritize multiple responsibilities while ensuring that important admission tasks are completed accurately and efficiently. I am comfortable communicating with patients, families, and healthcare professionals and understand the importance of maintaining professionalism, empathy, and confidentiality in every interaction.

Although I have not yet held a remote-work position, I do have experience with remote distance education and understand the self-discipline, motivation, and time-management skills required to be successful in that environment. I obtained my certification in Medical Office Administration while working part-time and raising three children on my own. I also earned my TEFL (Teaching English as a Foreign Language) certification through remote learning. These accomplishments demonstrate my ability to manage competing responsibilities, work independently, stay focused, and successfully complete goals through dedication and perseverance. I am confident that these qualities will translate well into a virtual work environment.

I am knowledgeable about HIPAA regulations and committed to protecting sensitive patient information. My years of experience in healthcare have taught me the importance of attention to detail, teamwork, discretion, and providing a positive experience for every patient and family.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and passion for healthcare administration to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I believe my background, strong work ethic, and willingness to learn would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your admissions team while supporting your mission of helping adolescents and their families access the care they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications can benefit your organization.

Sincerely,

Kimberlee Woodliffe

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. With more than 15 years of experience across mortgage services, general management, and the service industry, I bring a strong foundation in communication, organization, relationship-building, and compassionate client support. More importantly, I bring a personal understanding of how deeply mental health and addiction can affect individuals, families, and entire communities.

Throughout my professional career, I have developed the ability to connect with people from all walks of life, listen to their needs, navigate challenging conversations, and help guide them through important decisions. My background in mortgage services has taught me the importance of patience, attention to detail, and helping people navigate complicated and sometimes stressful circumstances. My management and service industry experience have strengthened my ability to multitask, communicate effectively, remain composed under pressure, and make people feel heard and valued.

My interest in this position is also deeply personal. I have navigated my own mental health journey and have had the privilege of knowing many people who have fought through addiction and pursued sobriety. Recently, I experienced the heartbreaking loss of my best friend of 23 years to an overdose. Their struggle with addiction was deeply connected to childhood trauma and abuse. That loss has reinforced my belief that early intervention, compassionate support, and access to the right resources can make a life-changing difference.

I know firsthand that behind every struggle is a person deserving of understanding, dignity, and the opportunity for a better future. I would be honored to play a part in helping adolescents and their families find hope, access meaningful treatment, and recognize that their circumstances today do not have to define their tomorrow. Finding a future worth living for is something I believe everyone deserves the opportunity to experience.

I understand that an Admissions Coordinator is often one of the first points of contact for families navigating some of the most difficult and emotional moments of their lives. I would approach that responsibility with empathy, professionalism, patience, and genuine care. I believe my professional background, interpersonal strengths, and personal perspective would allow me to contribute meaningfully to your team and the families you serve.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about how my experience, dedication, and passion for helping others could contribute to the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy. I would be proud to help make a difference in the lives of young people and help families find a path forward when they need it most.

Warm regards,

Reid L Golding

Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am reaching out because I would love the opportunity to join your team. For the past twelve years, my work and life have centered around supporting young people and their families through education, psychology and community work. When I came across this opening at Adolescent Wellness Academy, it immediately caught my attention because it aligns so closely with what I already care about and do every day.
Working in schools and special education for over a decade has taught me how to stay calm, adapt on the fly and truly connect with kids and teens from all walks of life. Alongside my classroom experience, my studies in clinical psychology and applied behavior analysis have helped me better understand what drives behavior and how to support youth through tough moments. Outside of work, I spend a lot of my time organizing local community outreach, mentorship, and family support efforts. I genuinely enjoy meeting new people, hearing their stories, and helping them figure out their next steps.
That same mindset carries over into my customer service background. Whether I am talking to a parent who feels overwhelmed, answering questions for a family, or working alongside a team, I always try to bring warmth, patience, and a steady presence to the room. People tend to feel comfortable opening up to me, and I take pride in making sure they feel heard and supported.
I also want to be completely honest about my administrative background. I have not worked directly in insurance billing before, though I do have plenty of experience writing detailed session notes specifically geared toward insurance billing requirements. I know how much accurate documentation matters behind the scenes. Because I am really excited about this position, I am already taking the initiative to research and learn the basics of behavioral health billing right now so I will not be starting from scratch.
If you bring me onto your team, you will get someone who is trustworthy, dependable, and comfortable working independently without needing to be micromanaged. I show up, do what needs to be done, and step in wherever I am needed. Thank you so much for taking the time to read this, and I look forward to speaking with you all soon.
Sincerely,
Demetria Evans

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a background in management, healthcare, rehabilitation, and administrative operations, I believe I bring a unique combination of leadership experience, compassion, strong communication skills, and the ability to work independently that would make me a strong addition to your team.

Throughout my career, I have worked in environments where compassion, professionalism, attention to detail, and the ability to navigate challenging situations are essential. My experience working in drug and alcohol rehabilitation gave me exposure to the importance of supportive care and the impact that treatment can have on individuals and families. I understand that reaching out for help can be overwhelming, and I would approach every interaction with patience, empathy, respect, and a genuine desire to help people navigate the next steps in accessing care.

My management experience has strengthened my ability to multitask, prioritize competing demands, maintain accurate documentation, communicate effectively, and follow through on responsibilities. I am comfortable learning new systems, working with sensitive information, and maintaining professionalism in fast-paced environments where accuracy and organization are critical.

I also bring experience working in hybrid and remote environments and am confident in my ability to manage my workload independently while remaining communicative, dependable, and accountable. I am proactive about staying organized, following through on outstanding tasks, managing deadlines, and ensuring that nothing falls through the cracks. I understand that remote work requires discipline, initiative, strong time management, and the ability to take ownership of your responsibilities, all of which I have developed throughout my management career.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it combines healthcare, meaningful human connection, organization, and the opportunity to make a difference in someone’s life. I am looking to transition my management and healthcare experience into a role where I can continue supporting others while contributing my administrative, communication, and operational strengths. I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my experience, work ethic, compassion, and dedication to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills could contribute to the success of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Best,
Bailey Jallo, CVT

To Whom concern ,

I'm excited to apply for the Virtual admissions  coordinator position. What I'd bring to this role is simple: I listen first, I know how to navigate EOB, claims ,referrals  and coverage details without losing sight of the person on the other end, and I don't consider a case done until it's actually taken care of. I'd welcome the chance to bring that same care to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,

30 S. Shell Rd.
DeBary, FL  32713

November 19, 2026

RE:  Opportunity at Adolescent Wellness Academy
Dear Hiring Team,
I am very interested in the position with as an Adolescent Wellness Assistant.  I have always enjoyed counseling and consoling people.  I have been a fearless Women’s Ministry leader at my church since 1999, Faith Assembly of God.  I have participated in motivational speaking opportunities to over 250 women on more than 7 occasions on how to move forward after hitting rock bottom.  I have spoken at conferences and been a Women’s Ministry leader assisting hundreds of women in gaining life skills, coping skills, and accepting responsibility skills.  I have always been interested in counseling as a career.  I have conducted psychotherapy sessions for 10 years at my church with hundreds of elderly and young women.
I took a People Helper Course, 50 hours, back in 1995-1996 and loved it!  I spent a year online counseling people both men and women.  I enjoyed counseling so much that I spent over 100 hours volunteering.  However, I had always wanted to be a teacher, so I went into the field of education.  I was awarded the Sallie Mae Teacher of the Year my first year of teaching.  I’ve been teaching for 27 years, and I want to change careers.  
The program you are using to help students sounds like a perfect fit for me.  Even though my degrees are in education AA, BS, MS, and Ed.S is in Curriculum & Instruction.  I have life experiences writing IEPs and tracking student information with data-driven instruction in curriculum and assessment.  My 27 years as a teacher has afforded me numerous opportunities to work with children who are troubled, dismayed, and signs of lethality.  
I have participated in conducting individual, group, and/or family psychotherapy as indicated by diagnosis and individualized treatment plan through the conferences held at my church.  In addition, during counseling sessions (usually lasting 3 days), I have participated in conducting comprehensive assessment of psychiatric history (e.g., onset, course and effect of illness, past treatment and responses, and risk behaviors), mental status, and diagnosis; physical health; use of drugs or alcohol; education and employment; social development and functioning; activities of daily living (e.g., self-care, living situation, nutrition, money management); and family structure and relationships.  I can be relied on to maintain confidentiality and follow the rules and procedures.  
I am a self-motivated learner and consider myself a life-long learner.  I will continue to move forward taking courses as needed for this opportunity.  Please see my resume for a list of responsibilities and references.
Thank you for allowing me this opportunity for an interview to serve as the Virtual Admissions Coordinator with Adolescent Wellness Academy.  I am looking forward to hearing from you soon.      
Sincerely,
Darlene Gravenmier, Ed.S. Curriculum & Instruction

Sydney Rudel

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Specialized Associate’s Degree in Medical Assisting, extensive experience in healthcare administration and patient coordination, and over 15 years of customer service experience, I believe I bring a strong combination of medical knowledge, communication skills, and compassion that would make me an asset to your admissions team.

Throughout my healthcare career, I have worked in several specialty settings, including pain management, and wellness. My experience includes coordinating patient appointments and referrals, communicating with patients and providers, maintaining electronic medical records, handling confidential health information, and helping patients navigate the next steps in their care. I am familiar with EMR systems, Athena, medical terminology, HIPAA compliance, and the importance of accurate documentation and timely follow-up.

I understand that the admissions process is often someone’s first interaction with a healthcare organization, and that first impression matters. My background in both healthcare and customer service has taught me how to actively listen, establish trust, navigate sensitive conversations, and communicate information in a way that makes people feel comfortable and understood. My caregiving experience has further strengthened my patience, compassion, and ability to support individuals and families through challenging circumstances.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because of the meaningful work your programs provide to adolescents and adults seeking mental health and substance use treatment. I recognize that reaching out for help can be overwhelming, both for individuals and their loved ones. I would take that responsibility seriously by approaching every inquiry with empathy, professionalism, discretion, and a commitment to helping each caller find an appropriate next step.

I am organized, adaptable, self-motivated, and comfortable managing multiple responsibilities in fast paced environments. I understand the importance of maintaining accurate lead records, following up consistently, coordinating documentation, and ensuring that no inquiry falls through the cracks. I am confident in my ability to learn new systems and processes quickly while maintaining a high standard of patient communication and organization.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare background, administrative experience, and genuine passion for helping others to your growing team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how my qualifications could contribute to your admissions department.

Sincerely,

Christine Cushley

Chantilly McKinnon

Sherman, Texas

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor’s degree in social work and professional experience as an Eligibility Specialist with the Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC), I bring a strong background in client advocacy, service coordination, eligibility screening, confidential documentation, and connecting individuals and families with essential resources.

In my current role with HHSC, I work directly with individuals and families navigating complex and often stressful circumstances. I regularly assess individual needs, gather and evaluate sensitive information, explain eligibility requirements and available services, maintain accurate case documentation, and help individuals navigate systems that can otherwise feel overwhelming. This experience has strengthened my ability to communicate with compassion, exercise sound judgment, manage competing priorities, and ensure that people feel heard and supported throughout the process.

My educational background in social work has further developed my understanding of mental health, substance use, family dynamics, crisis situations, and the importance of meeting individuals where they are. I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because of its focus on helping adolescents and families access mental health treatment, as well as supporting individuals seeking recovery from substance use disorders. I believe that the first interaction someone has with a treatment provider can make a meaningful difference in whether they feel comfortable taking that next step toward receiving help.

I would bring a combination of empathy, professionalism, organization, and strong follow-through to your admissions team. I am comfortable handling sensitive conversations, gathering detailed information, maintaining confidentiality, navigating complex administrative processes, and communicating information in a way that is clear and approachable. I also understand the importance of accurate documentation, timely follow-up, and treating every individual and family with dignity and respect.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my social work education, public service experience, and passion for helping individuals and families to your organization. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills could contribute to your admissions team and the individuals you serve.

Sincerely,

Chantilly McKinnon

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in medical administration and patient care, I have developed a genuine appreciation for the importance of compassionate communication, organization, and helping individuals navigate what can often be an overwhelming healthcare system.

In my previous role as a Medical Receptionist in a busy primary care practice, I was responsible for patient scheduling, insurance verification, coordinating referrals, managing patient communications, and maintaining accurate records through Epic EHR. I regularly assisted patients who were frustrated, confused, or anxious about their care, and I learned how important it is to approach each interaction with patience, empathy, and a willingness to find solutions.

Additionally, my experience as a full-time caregiver strengthened my ability to support individuals through vulnerable and challenging circumstances. These experiences have taught me to remain calm under pressure, communicate clearly, and recognize that even the smallest interactions can make a meaningful difference in someone's day.

What particularly draws me to this opportunity is the chance to be a supportive first point of contact for individuals and families seeking mental health or substance use treatment. I understand that reaching out for help can be an incredibly difficult step, and I would take pride in helping make that experience feel less intimidating and more reassuring. I am also drawn to the opportunity to work independently while remaining connected to a team dedicated to helping people access the care they need.

Although my professional background has primarily been in primary care rather than behavioral health admissions, I am confident that my experience with patient coordination, insurance processes, electronic health records, and sensitive patient interactions has prepared me to transition successfully into this role. I am eager to expand my knowledge of behavioral health services and contribute to a team making such an important difference in people's lives.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, work ethic, and commitment to compassionate patient care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,  
Angela Balice

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to combine my professional experience in coordination and customer service with something I genuinely care about: helping individuals and families find the support and resources they need during some of the most difficult periods of their lives.

My interest in this field is also personal. Through my own life experiences, I understand how overwhelming it can be to navigate mental health challenges, search for appropriate treatment, locate community resources, and figure out where to turn when you don’t know what options are available. I know firsthand how much of a difference it can make when someone takes the time to listen, treats you with compassion rather than judgment, and helps you navigate the next steps. I would love the opportunity to be that person for families who may be feeling overwhelmed, scared, or unsure of where to begin.

Professionally, I bring a diverse background in customer service, independent operations, event coordination, and administrative responsibilities. In previous positions, I have been responsible for coordinating activities, communicating with a wide range of individuals, managing schedules and logistics, resolving problems, maintaining organization, and handling multiple responsibilities independently. I have also worked in roles requiring patience, adaptability, strong communication skills, and the ability to remain composed when situations become challenging.

I believe one of my greatest strengths is my ability to understand people without making assumptions about their circumstances. I recognize that every individual and family has a different story, and I would approach every interaction with empathy, patience, professionalism, and respect. I am also comfortable learning new systems, following established procedures, and taking initiative when something needs to be done.

I am looking for a long-term career where I can grow professionally while doing work that has a meaningful impact on other people’s lives. The opportunity to help adolescents and their families take the first steps toward receiving mental health and substance use treatment is something I would take seriously and approach with genuine compassion.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my professional background, personal perspective, and dedication to helping others could make me a valuable addition to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team.

Sincerely,
Amber

Victoria Welch

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With six years of experience in healthcare, including roles as a Surgery Coordinator and Ophthalmic Scribe, I have developed a strong background in patient communication, care coordination, scheduling, and administrative support. I am confident that my experience, attention to detail, and compassionate approach to patient care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Throughout my time as a Surgery Coordinator, I served as a primary point of contact for patients navigating the surgical process. My responsibilities included coordinating procedures, managing schedules, communicating with patients and medical providers, and ensuring all necessary documentation and preoperative requirements were completed. I understand how overwhelming medical decisions can feel, and I take pride in helping patients feel informed, comfortable, and supported throughout their care.

My experience as an Ophthalmic Scribe has further strengthened my ability to manage detailed medical records, navigate electronic medical record systems, maintain patient confidentiality, and communicate effectively within a fast-paced healthcare environment. These roles have taught me the importance of organization, accuracy, adaptability, and consistent follow-through.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to be a reassuring first point of contact for individuals and families seeking help. While my professional background has primarily been in ophthalmology, I believe the compassion, patience, and communication skills I have developed are directly transferable to admissions coordination. I recognize that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable experience, and I would approach every interaction with empathy, professionalism, and respect.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare experience, organizational skills, and dedication to patient-centered care to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,

Victoria Welch

candidates.cover_letter:
I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment position. With more than a decade of experience in juvenile intake, correctional mental health, crisis intervention, law enforcement, and working with individuals and families during challenging circumstances, I believe I bring a unique combination of professional experience, communication skills, and compassion that would make me a strong addition to your admissions team.

Throughout my career, I have worked with individuals facing difficult personal circumstances, behavioral challenges, mental health concerns, and situations requiring timely intervention and appropriate referrals. As a Juvenile Intake Officer with the Kansas 24th Judicial District, I regularly responded to law enforcement requests involving juvenile offenders and children in need of care. This required assessing circumstances, communicating with families and professionals, coordinating appropriate referrals and placements, and helping determine the next steps for young people during some of their most difficult moments.

My experience as a Corrections Counselor with the Kansas Department of Corrections further strengthened my ability to work with individuals experiencing behavioral and emotional challenges. I helped residents navigate difficult transitions, encouraged positive behavioral changes, supported treatment-related goals, and connected individuals with appropriate resources. I also served as a Due Process Coordinator at Larned State Hospital, where I worked within a mental health treatment environment while maintaining accurate procedures, documentation, and compliance with established policies.

In my current role as a police officer, I continue to rely on strong communication, sound judgment, de-escalation, and the ability to build rapport with people from different backgrounds and circumstances. Outside of law enforcement, my experience as a middle school basketball coach has strengthened my passion for mentoring adolescents, building trust, encouraging positive decisions, and helping young people recognize their potential.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to make a meaningful difference before someone even enters treatment. Although I am transitioning from a different industry, I am confident that my communication skills, attention to detail, willingness to learn, and educational background would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Abrial Coleman

I am comfortable navigating multiple EMR systems, verifying insurance coverage, coordinating referrals, obtaining prior authorizations, and maintaining accurate patient records. As a bilingual professional fluent in English and Spanish, I can effectively communicate with a diverse patient population and help patients and families feel comfortable and understood.

I would appreciate the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and passion for patient care to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my background and skills can contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Esilda Prentice, CCMA

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining your organization and contributing my experience, knowledge, and passion for behavioral health and substance use recovery services.

I believe one of my greatest strengths is my ability to connect with people while maintaining professionalism, accountability, and compassion. I am looking for an opportunity where I can contribute my experience, continue developing professionally, and make a meaningful difference in the lives of the individuals and communities being served. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience could benefit your team.

Richard Webster

work_history.title: Senior Recovery Coach/Family Recovery Coach
work_history.company_name: Lowell House Addiction Treatment and Recovery
work_history.summary: Certified CCAR Recovery Coach. Working on a peer to peer platform that is fully Recoveree based. I conduct meetings in office and out in the community. I help everyone from active addicts to those with 20+ years of sobriety, and I help them figure out "what is next". Stopping the use of substances is a monumentally positive achievement and very hard to maintain. That being said, life does not slow down before, during, or after active use. I am here to support and help any and all Recoverees no matter what stage they are at to make their lives manageable. I often get the question, "I stopped doing drugs, that is great, now what?" or "how do i fix all the issues I have created from my substance use?" and this is exactly where I come in as a Recovery Coach. Any and all questions I find answers for. If I cannot answer it myself I will find the appropriate person who can. It is also important to say that I actually do not DO any of the work for a Recoveree. They do all the work themselves, and I just provide guidance and tools. There's no mandatory ANYTHING with Recovery Coaching and that is how we meet the Recoveree where they are at. The recoveree creates a Wellness Plan with me and we track progress towards eat goal no matter what it is or how big or how small the progress might be. All of this while retraining the brain to ditch the "instant Gratification" mind set and molding a positive and personable personal atmosphere. There is no such thing as failure unless you give up and I am here to try anything and everything to get a person where they really want to be and push past their idea of potential and into a whole new realm of what they can do. This also comes with Insurance auth/reauth services, Billing setups, intake/discharge documentation, avid computer skills for written documents, skills in the use of software for maintaining and organizing documentation, digital and paper documentation of all engagements, ESM Virtual Gateway Assessments for BSAS, communicating with other providers within the Recoveree's circle for integrated care, communicating with insurance companies to continue engagement in services, following HIPPA and 42 CFR guidelines and filling out appropriate Release Documentation, and all other forms and documentation required for confidentiality, referrals, and insurance/billing. I also possess logins for the Executive Office of Health and Human Services, and all insurance companies under the MA Health umbrella. I report to a supervisor who previously had my position but is now the Director of a Peer Center owned and operated by LHI and funded by BSAS so I am the only member of my department not in management. I was tasked with writing the entire operational process from start to finish, meeting a client for the first time to discharging after completion, and ALL the processes in-between. This includes the billing, insurance, contact documentation, filing forms for HIPPA and 42 CFR, all the guidelines for BSAS and MA Health Insurance. These book only pertains to the processes of Recovery Coaching specifically at Lowell House Addiction Treatment and Recovery. I will be with Lowell House Addiction Treatment and Recovery for 2 years as of June 2021and hope to be promoted to the Recovery Coach Supervisor for all new interns and New Hires as they will be using the book I created to learn how to do the job. I have conducted all aspects of the job in both in person/office atmospheres as well as at home from a laptop for administrative work and virtually for contacts and meets through multiple platforms such as ZOOM and Goggle Meets.

Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a background in psychology, current graduate studies in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and professional experience in behavioral health intake, client coordination, and community-based services, I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your admissions team.

Through my work with Nurturing Hearts Services, I have developed experience supporting behavioral health intake, coordinating services with individuals and families, maintaining confidential client documentation, and communicating with support coordinators and external agencies. I have also participated in individualized service planning and ongoing coordination of care for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to approach sensitive situations with professionalism, empathy, discretion, and attention to detail.

In addition to my direct experience in community-based care, I bring a strong administrative background and the ability to manage responsibilities independently in a remote work environment. My experience includes coordinating schedules, maintaining records, managing correspondence, and supporting program operations. I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. As a psychology graduate and mental health professional, I am passionate about creating meaningful connections with individuals and families while helping them access the care and support they deserve.

As I continue to build my career in mental health, I am eager to pursue opportunities that align with my passion for supporting adolescents, advocating for accessible treatment, and making a meaningful difference in the lives of others. Jada E. Thompson, B.S. Psychology

Serving as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator requires more than administrative precision—it demands active listening, genuine empathy, and the ability to build immediate trust over the phone or screen. Throughout my career, I have developed a strong foundation in these exact areas:
• Empathetic Family & Client Rapport: Experienced in de-escalating crisis moments, listening without judgment, and reassuring anxious parents and caregivers while clearly explaining program options and next steps.
• Seamless Intake & Insurance Navigation: Skilled at conducting thorough initial assessments, verifying insurance benefits accurately, coordinating with clinical teams for level-of-care approvals, and maintaining strict HIPAA compliance in a remote environment.
• Persistent, Organized Follow-Through: Proven ability to manage a high volume of inquiries in CRM and EHR systems, ensuring timely follow-ups so no teen or family falls through the cracks during the critical window between first contact and admission.
Working remotely requires strong self-direction and seamless communication with multidisciplinary teams. My background bridging front-line support and healthcare administration allows me to collaborate effortlessly with clinicians, utilization review specialists, and outreach teams to ensure every transition into care is as smooth and stress-free as possible.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my dedication to behavioral health advocacy, rapport building, and admissions coordination can help Adolescent Wellness Academy connect more teens and families with life-changing care. I can be reached at 812-653-6468 or richardsonfancy@gmail.com to schedule an interview.  

With Gratitude 
Nancy M Richardson

To whom it may concern, 

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. As a bilingual English-Spanish professional, virtual Spanish language instructor, and student pursuing an Associate of Applied Science in Human Services with a concentration in Addictions Counseling, I am passionate about supporting individuals and families navigating behavioral health challenges and accessing appropriate treatment.

My professional background includes experience in residential treatment environments, where I developed an appreciation for trauma-informed care, compassionate communication, and the importance of establishing trust with vulnerable populations. My academic studies continue to strengthen my understanding of substance use disorders, behavioral health, and individualized, person-centered approaches to care.

Additionally, through my work as a virtual Spanish language instructor, I independently coordinate online learning sessions, develop individualized educational materials, communicate with families, and facilitate engaging instruction in a remote environment. This experience has strengthened my organizational abilities, technological adaptability, time management, and capacity to establish meaningful professional relationships through virtual communication. My instructional philosophy emphasizes connection before correction, recognizing that effective communication begins with empathy, patience, and an understanding of individual needs.

I am also pursuing education in medical billing and coding, further expanding my understanding of healthcare administration, medical terminology, insurance processes, and accurate, confidential documentation. Together, these educational and professional experiences have equipped me with a multidisciplinary perspective that I believe would translate effectively into behavioral health admissions coordination.

On a personal level, navigating a complex healthcare journey as the parent of a medically complex child has strengthened my advocacy skills, resilience, and ability to communicate with multidisciplinary healthcare teams. This experience has deepened my understanding of the uncertainty families may experience when seeking specialized care and reinforced my commitment to ensuring individuals feel heard, respected, and supported throughout the process.

I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to serve as an initial point of contact for adolescents, adults, and families seeking behavioral health treatment. I recognize the importance of approaching these conversations with professionalism, cultural sensitivity, discretion, and compassion. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my bilingual communication skills, remote instructional experience, educational foundation, and commitment to behavioral healthcare to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to further discuss how my qualifications and dedication to service align with your organization’s mission.

Sincerely,
Allisson Harris

Jermiane Rodriguez
New Braunfels,Texas
Jermrazorod@icloud.com
(210) 917-7557

November 17, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Science in Human and Community Advocacy from the University of Texas at San Antonio, an Associate of Arts in Psychology, and professional experience in healthcare, customer service, and public assistance, I bring a combination of professional qualifications, compassion, and a genuine commitment to helping adolescents and families access mental health services.

Throughout my career, including my work with Texas Health and Human Services, healthcare-related call centers, and my current position with Aflac, I have developed strong skills in communication, active listening, documentation, problem-solving, and assisting individuals through complex and sometimes emotionally challenging situations. My experience has taught me the importance of maintaining confidentiality, gathering accurate information, explaining processes clearly, and ensuring that individuals feel respected and supported.

What makes this opportunity particularly meaningful to me is my personal experience as a mother who has navigated the mental health system while advocating for a child experiencing significant emotional and behavioral health challenges. I understand firsthand the fear, uncertainty, and emotional exhaustion that families can experience when trying to find appropriate treatment. My family has navigated hospitalizations, mental health crises, and community-based behavioral health services, including the YES Waiver program. Through those experiences, I witnessed how compassionate professionals can make an extraordinary difference in the lives of both adolescents and their families.

Those experiences strengthened my desire to pursue a career in mental health advocacy. They also taught me the importance of listening without judgment, communicating with empathy, and helping families feel supported during some of their most vulnerable moments. I recognize that an admissions coordinator may be one of the first people a struggling adolescent or concerned parent speaks with, and I would approach that responsibility with professionalism, patience, compassion, and respect.

I am particularly interested in the opportunity to assist families throughout the admissions process, coordinate necessary information, communicate with treatment teams, and help individuals better understand their options for care. My background in telephone-based customer service, healthcare documentation, insurance-related inquiries, and administrative support would allow me to contribute meaningfully while continuing to develop my knowledge of adolescent mental health and substance use treatment.

As I pursue my long-term goal of earning a Master of Social Work, I am seeking an opportunity where my professional skills and personal passion can come together to make a meaningful difference. I would be honored to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s work supporting adolescents and helping families find hope, guidance, and access to appropriate treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education, experience, and dedication to mental health advocacy would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Jermiane Rodriguez

Abigail Cornele

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Mooresville, NC

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Social Worker Associate (LCSWA) with a Master of Social Work degree and three years of experience supporting children, adolescents, and families, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to AWA's mission of providing compassionate, evidence-based mental health services to adolescents. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to join the founding clinical team and help establish a supportive, collaborative, and client-centered therapeutic environment.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed a strong foundation in family-centered treatment, crisis intervention, case management, treatment planning, and trauma-informed care. In my current role as a Family Centered Treatment Specialist with Pinnacle Family Services, I provide individualized treatment and case management services to children and families in home and community settings. I develop treatment plans, facilitate interventions, collaborate with community partners, and support families in navigating challenges while promoting stability, resilience, and improved outcomes. This experience has strengthened my ability to build therapeutic relationships, identify individual and family needs, and implement interventions that support meaningful behavioral and emotional change.

Previously, as a Family Advocate at Pat's Place Child Advocacy Center, I supported children and families navigating difficult and often traumatic circumstances. I provided emotional support, crisis intervention, resource coordination, and advocacy while collaborating with multidisciplinary professionals to prioritize child safety and family well-being. My school social work experience at Hawthorne Academy further strengthened my ability to recognize and address the emotional, behavioral, academic, and social needs of at-risk students while developing interventions and connecting families with appropriate resources.

I believe my background in child and family services provides a valuable foundation for working with adolescents experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, behavioral challenges, and other mental health concerns. I am passionate about creating a therapeutic space where adolescents feel safe, understood, and empowered to develop healthy coping strategies and recognize their strengths. I also understand the importance of family involvement, interdisciplinary collaboration, individualized treatment planning, and consistent communication in supporting successful clinical outcomes.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical experience, dedication to family-centered care, and passion for adolescent mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Being part of a new program would allow me to contribute not only to the care of adolescents and their families but also to the development of a positive clinical culture built on compassion, collaboration, and excellence.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications, experience, and commitment to serving children and families would make me a valuable addition to AWA's founding clinical team.

Sincerely,

Abigail Cornele, MSW, LCSWA

candidates.cover_letter:
Hareesma Amutha Venkatesan
Charlotte, NC
980-408-9604 | hareesma@yahoo.com

November 18, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Mooresville, North Carolina

Re: Operations Manager, Behavioral Health

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Operations Manager position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. What particularly attracted me to this opportunity is the chance to be part of a founding team and help establish a supportive, well-organized environment for adolescents and their families. With a Master’s degree in Counselling Psychology, two years of full-time experience working directly with mental health clients, and a background in operations management, staff supervision, and business administration, I believe I can bring a valuable combination of clinical understanding and operational leadership to your new North Carolina location.

As the founder of HAP TherapyCare, I independently established and managed a virtual psychotherapy practice while providing direct mental health services. Beyond working with clients, I was responsible for nearly every aspect of running the practice, including client inquiries, intake, scheduling, billing, clinical documentation, professional referrals, and maintaining appropriate standards of confidentiality and care. This experience gave me an appreciation for how much the quality of a client’s experience depends on what happens behind the scenes. Clear communication, reliable processes, timely follow-up, and a welcoming environment can make a meaningful difference for individuals and families seeking support.

My operational leadership experience extends beyond healthcare. At Toronto Inspection Ltd., I coordinated 10 to 15 field technicians and more than 20 daily site visits across multiple active projects while guiding administrative staff, resolving escalations, and improving documentation processes. I regularly investigated complex operational and billing discrepancies, worked with different stakeholders to identify solutions, and introduced practical improvements to make daily operations more organized and efficient. I also bring experience in employee recruitment, interviewing, onboarding, training, and supervision, along with additional business administration and payroll responsibilities through my work with Saphgen.

One quality I would particularly bring to Adolescent Wellness Academy is a strong sense of ownership. When something is not working, I naturally want to understand why, explore possible solutions, and follow through until the issue is addressed. I enjoy creating structure, supporting colleagues, and finding ways to make people’s work easier without losing sight of the individuals we serve. My counselling background has also shaped how I lead and communicate, with empathy, patience, accountability, and respect for different perspectives.

I understand that launching a new behavioral health clinic requires flexibility, collaboration, and attention to both operational details and the experiences of clients, families, and staff. Although I have not previously managed an adolescent PHP or IOP program, I am eager to build on my existing experience, learn the specific requirements of your programs, and contribute to establishing strong operational foundations from the beginning.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in mental health services, practice management, and operational leadership could support Adolescent Wellness Academy’s expansion into North Carolina. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your team.

Sincerely,
Hareesma Amutha Venkatesan
